title: Remove Codebase Memory MCP from Sinnix
description: Codebase Memory MCP repeatedly grows until it saturates the agent scope. The latest orphaned process consumed 8.3 GiB RSS and 12.4 GiB swap, causing severe system-wide I/O stalls. Remove the server, package, UI service, profiles, wrappers, and documentation entirely.
design: Delete the capability rather than adding another resource limit or compatibility shim. Serena remains the semantic edit/navigation MCP; rg remains exact search.
acceptance_criteria: No Sinnix agent, VS Code profile, package export, user service, status tool, sweep rule, test, or documentation references Codebase Memory MCP; the live process is gone; switch deploys the removal; agent profile tests and lint pass.
close_reason: Killed the 8.3 GiB runaway MCP process, removed Codebase Memory from registry, packages, profiles, UI service, persistence, editor config, tooling, tests, and docs, detached the obsolete mount, verified generated profiles, and deployed the removal.

title: Screenshot capture (grim/grimblast) produces pure-black frames — GBM XR30 allocation failure on nvidia-drm backend
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-02/03: every screencopy capture of the DP-3 output (AORUS FO48U OLED, 4K120 10-bit HDR) via grim/grimblast/sinnix-screenshot-control produces a PNG with all-zero pixels (min=max=mean=0 across every channel, verified via `identify -verbose`) -- not washed out, not corrupted, genuinely empty.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via Hyprland log): GBM buffer allocation fails for the 10-bit XR30 format, recurring throughout the entire session log (12+ occurrences, effectively every capture attempt):

    ERR from aquamarine ]: GBM: Failed to allocate a GBM buffer: format XR30 isn't supported by primary backend

The compositor does not surface this as a visible error to the capturing client -- screencopy "succeeds" (grim exits 0, produces a non-empty file) but the returned buffer content is empty/zeroed instead of the real framebuffer.

Contributing factor: `GBM_BACKEND = "nvidia-drm"` is explicitly set in hosts/sinnix-prime/display.nix (lines 53 and 140). Current driver: 595.84 (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version`). This matches a known category of upstream issues where an NVIDIA driver update breaks GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm support for specific buffer formats (see hyprwm/Hyprland#1878 for a related historical instance, though not an exact match for this XR30-specific failure).

NOT a Hyprland render-pipeline config issue: toggling `render:cm_enabled` live (true/false) does NOT fix the black frames either way -- tested both, `grim -o DP-3` still returns all-zero pixels with cm_enabled=false, contradicting dots/_ai/skills/desktop-control-plane/references/hdr-screenshots.md's claim ("with render:cm_enabled=false ... direct grim screencopy ... yields correct sRGB frames, no black frames") -- that doc is now STALE/WRONG against the current driver/runtime state and needs correcting once this is actually fixed, not just re-verified.

NOT the inactive-window-opacity issue (checked while investigating, unrelated): `sdr_min_luminance = 0.2` and `decoration:inactive_opacity = 0.75` are both correctly live and matching hosts/sinnix-prime/display.nix's intended config right now -- if translucency still looks insufficient to the operator that's a value-tuning preference question, not a misconfiguration bug.

WHY QEMU VM TESTING DOESN'T APPLY (operator called this out correctly): this bug is a real GPU/driver/panel interaction (NVIDIA RTX 3080 + 10-bit HDR OLED panel + GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm), not reproducible in a virtualized GPU environment. Any fix needs to be tested against the real hardware, live, with the understanding that a wrong change could require a Hyprland restart (relogin) to recover -- this is NOT a change to test-vm first.

SUGGESTED INVESTIGATION PATH (not yet attempted, needs live testing with explicit operator go-ahead per the risk above):
1. Try removing `GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm` entirely (both occurrences in display.nix) and see if the default GBM backend selection handles XR30 allocation correctly, OR
2. Check if there's a newer/different driver version that resolves this specific format-support regression, OR
3. Check whether forcing screencopy/capture clients specifically (not the whole compositor) to request an 8-bit format instead of the output's native 10-bit works around it without sacrificing the display's actual HDR/10-bit rendering for normal use.

Operator explicitly deferred live testing of any of these -- filed as P0 documentation for now, to be tested/fixed in a dedicated session with the operator present at the physical machine (not remotely, given the relogin-risk).
close_reason: Superseded by the deployed HDR capture path: Hyprland retains an unmodified screencopy frame, Print uses Noctalia native capture, and current diagnostic grim/grimblast raw captures are non-black (16-bit max 65535, mean about 15286). The underlying intermittent upstream HDR screencopy behavior remains documented, but the Sinnix capture workflow no longer produces black frames.

title: Scrub publication-sensitive historical surfaces
description: Remove obsolete or overly specific historical configuration and documentation from every reachable public commit, preserve the intended current tree, and verify that only the authoritative master ref remains publishable.
acceptance_criteria: Requested historical surfaces are unreachable from master; the private report is retained in the operator knowledgebase; current intentional configuration remains coherent; the rewritten signed master is the only public ref upstream.
notes: 2026-07-13 follow-up: a stale Beads export reintroduced an overly specific operational record at the signed tip. The live Beads source was sanitized first, then the same generic record was propagated through every historical JSONL version so future exports cannot restore the disclosure.
close_reason: History-wide publication cleanup verified in a fresh single-ref replay; private source retained outside the public repository.

title: Contain runaway agent subprocesses before global OOM
description:
## Incident
On 2026-07-12 18:23:55, a recursive agent-launched ugrep reached 15,863 MiB RSS. agent.slice and every transient agent scope had MemoryHigh/MemoryMax=infinity and no ManagedOOM policy. earlyoom's --avoid regex matched the child comm claude.exe, so it killed 58 smaller unavoided processes first, including start-hyprland, before killing the actual hog. RAM fell below 3% available and both 12 GiB zram plus 8 GiB NVMe swap were exhausted.

## Scope
Install per-agent-scope memory containment through the shared runtime inventory and sinnix-scope path; remove generic agent/runtime/browser immunity from global earlyoom while retaining recovery-critical desktop/control-plane protection; verify live under a safe low-limit synthetic scope. Preserve the ability to run legitimate builds by routing them to build/nix-build scopes and preserve explicit per-job agent overrides.

## Non-goals
Do not restore a shared agent.slice cap that can freeze all agents together. Do not add MemorySwapMax. Do not permanently reduce build parallelism or feature coverage. Do not rely on process-name matching as the primary containment boundary.
design: Use per-transient-scope defaults (MemoryHigh=8G, MemoryMax=12G), not a shared agent.slice ceiling. Keep OOMPolicy=stop so an unreclaimable memcg OOM sacrifices the affected agent scope. Do not place OOMScoreAdjust in the scope inventory: live verification proved systemd rejects it for transient .scope units; victim preference belongs only on service/process launch surfaces. Narrow earlyoom --avoid to recovery-critical system/session surfaces; at the -m3 emergency floor agents and browsers must be eligible victims. The cgroup boundary is primary; earlyoom is only a last-resort backstop.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every newly launched Claude/Codex/Gemini agent scope receives finite default MemoryHigh and MemoryMax from runtime-defaults, with explicit per-job overrides still winning. 2. A single agent has MemoryMax=12 GiB and pressure begins at 8 GiB, while agent.slice itself remains uncapped to avoid cross-agent freeze coupling. 3. earlyoom no longer avoids claude/codex/node/python/chrome or generic shells; recovery-critical compositor/session/control-plane processes remain protected including start-hyprland. The scope inventory excludes properties systemd does not accept on .scope units. 4. A regression check evaluates the generated runtime policy and earlyoom pattern, failing on infinite agent scope limits, invalid OOMScoreAdjust, or renewed generic agent immunity. 5. After switch, systemctl shows the live defaults on a fresh agent scope; a safe low-limit synthetic scope demonstrates MemoryHigh containment without terminating Hyprland. 6. The 2026-07-12 incident evidence and before/after receipts are recorded durably.
notes: 2026-07-12 implementation/verification: incident journals show PID 3404367 recursive ugrep at 15,863 MiB RSS in an unbounded agent scope; earlyoom sent 59 victim signals and killed start-hyprland before the hog. Added inventory-owned per-agent MemoryHigh=8G/MemoryMax=12G while leaving agent.slice infinity; narrowed earlyoom avoid regex to recovery-critical processes. Live switch succeeded through the exact-toplevel fallback after the ordinary activation path hit the pre-existing dbus-broker reload failure. Fresh sinnix-agent-policy-probe.scope showed Slice=agent.slice, MemoryHigh=8589934592, MemoryMax=12884901888, IOWeight=300. A first probe exposed OOMScoreAdjust as invalid for transient scopes; removed it and added a regression assertion before final activation. Safe MemoryHigh=64M probe peaked at 64.2M resident plus 101.3M swap and left Hyprland PID 3409789 alive, demonstrating bounded resident pressure without restoring the historically brittle production MemorySwapMax. Exact checks: nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.agent-resource-policy --no-link; nix eval --json .#nixosConfigurations.sinnix-prime.config.sinnix.runtime.inventory.commandClasses.agent.systemdProperties; nix develop --command lint; nix develop --command switch; live systemctl/journal probes. Incident artifacts: /realm/tmp/earlyoom-incident-20260712-1823.log, /realm/tmp/system-incident-20260712-1823.log, /realm/tmp/cgtop-after-oom-20260712.txt.
close_reason: Deployed and verified per-agent 8G/12G containment plus recovery-focused earlyoom fallback; live probe caught and removed an invalid scope property before closure.

title: Keep GPU VLM devshells outside the heavy lease
description: The Sinnix direnv nix wrapper classifies every nix invocation as nix-build, so a long-running GPU VLM service launched with nix develop acquires the global heavyweight lease and blocks switch. Add an explicit accelerated-runtime command class and route the VLM devshell commands into it without weakening build and Nix lease enforcement. Add regression coverage for the wrapper classification and inventory policy.
acceptance_criteria: VLM devshell launches do not acquire the heavyweight lease; switch and Nix build commands still require the lease; focused tests pass.
notes: Implemented gpu-runtime command classification for stashbox VLM devshells; live switch succeeded with local Polylogue override; VLM verified in gpu-runtime.slice with no heavy lease while nix-build remains lease-required.
close_reason: GPU VLM launches now use gpu-runtime without the heavy lease; focused checks, live switch, and live cgroup/lease verification passed.

title: Generate the sinnix-prime capability and lifecycle manifest
description: Reconcile the corrected comprehensive handoff against current master and the live sinnix-prime machine. Generate one truthful capability/lifecycle manifest from the existing feature tree, package declarations, runtime inventory, systemd units, capture producers, persistent roots, endpoints, and observed state. Classify facilities as substrate, capture, scheduled, on-demand, interactive, manual, dormant, broken, or obsolete. Preserve broad Prime capability and default-on feature semantics. Treat sinnix-ethereal as dormant source outside the Prime critical path. Do not create a second runtime registry, host-role abstraction, or least-privilege agent profile.
design: Extend the existing runtime inventory and source declarations rather than adding a parallel registry. Start from the current live census and evaluated Prime declarations, record declaration versus current-generation versus live-state evidence, and make the manifest diff reviewable. A stopped service is not unused by itself. Every removal or default cleanup requires capability-preservation proof. Keep capture default-on and make stale or missing producers explicit. The corrected handoff archive is design input only; re-read current Beads and source before each mutation.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned Prime capability/lifecycle manifest is generated from existing authorities; every declared feature, service, socket, timer, capture producer, persistent root, endpoint, and resident process is classified or explicitly unknown with evidence; live state and current-generation drift are distinguished; Ethereal is marked dormant or outside ordinary Prime gates; manifest changes have a reviewable diff; no duplicate registry, host-role migration, capability deletion, capture opt-out, or local-agent restriction is introduced; focused checks and a live verification pass are recorded.
notes:
Imported viable scope from sinnix-comprehensive-handoff-corrected v2 on 2026-08-07. The supplied read-only census reached host, repository, runtime, storage, backup, and local-AI captures but failed before final archive/index generation after a long filesystem walk; partial evidence is preserved under /realm/tmp/work/sinnix-comprehensive-audit-20260807. The handoff's broad Prime capability, broad local authority, absolute capture, Sinex convergence, and quiescent multi-backend AI constraints are binding design input, subject to current-source/live verification.

Files changed:
- scripts/sinnix-capability-manifest: derived JSON report joining source feature/service/script declarations, runtime inventory surfaces, live systemd ActiveState, source revision, deployed configuration revision, persistent/runtime path references, explicit unknowns, and dormant Ethereal classification.
- modules/runtime.nix: install the command in the live system profile.
- flake/packages.nix: expose the public package.
- flake/tests.nix and flake/tests/capability-manifest.nix: fixture verifies feature, service, script, surface, unknown, schema, and dormant-host behavior.

- Feature/service/script declarations and runtime surfaces: satisfied. Live result contains 47 feature modules, 29 service modules, 72 scripts, and 47 runtime surfaces.
- Declaration versus live state: satisfied. Each runtime surface carries runtime-inventory evidence and live-systemd state where queried; source revision and configuration revision are separate fields.
- Ethereal: satisfied as explicit dormant source outside Prime live state.
- Unknown evidence: satisfied. One explicit service-source-to-runtime-surface unknown category remains rather than being inferred false or unused.

Verification:

No live service lifecycle was changed. Protected dirty paths modules/services/polylogue.nix and .beads/dolt-server-config.yaml remain untouched.

title: Normalize provider quota snapshots and windows
description: Create the quota ingestion substrate consumed by the operator reducer and fleet UI. Keep provider quota, local tokens, and API-equivalent cost as separate quantities with explicit source, freshness, account, plan epoch, and uncertainty.
design: Package an exact reviewed CodexBar Linux CLI release as the first adapter. Prefer provider CLI, OAuth, or app-server data on Linux and record when browser-backed modes are unavailable. Evaluate coding_agent_usage_tracker, whose executable is caut, as an independent canary after its schema and provider parity are measured. Keep ccusage and Polylogue as local-usage evidence only. Normalize account hashes, plans, plan epochs, fixed or rolling windows, used and remaining fractions, reset time, native units, source, fetched time, stale threshold, confidence, and coverage. Preserve append-only raw adapter payloads with secrets removed before normalization. Add 5-minute, 15-minute, 1-hour, and whole-window burn views only when the source cadence supports them. Unknown or stale never becomes zero.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded Codex and at least one non-Codex fixture normalize into one versioned schema; provider quota, local token categories, and calculated cost remain separate; account or plan changes start a new plan epoch; stale and unsupported Linux acquisition are explicit; raw redacted snapshots can regenerate normalized rows; CodexBar and caut disagreement is visible rather than averaged away; secrets and account identifiers are absent from published artifacts; focused adapter and migration tests pass.
notes: Implemented and deployed the quota ingestion substrate. Changed files: pkgs/sinnix-quota/pkg.nix, pyproject.toml, sinnix_quota/__init__.py, cli.py, normalize.py, tests/test_normalize.py; flake/scripts.nix; flake/tests.nix; flake/tests/quota.nix; modules/services/ops-reducer.nix. Acceptance matrix: CodexBar v0.47.0 Linux x86_64 is pinned by the official release asset and SRI hash sha256-Qv+L/3kDUHjJHIWdC9n3uvWCF8qYj6o9sHG/DICjAtU=, and at least one non-Codex caut.v1-shaped fixture normalize into sinnix-quota-v1 rows: satisfied. Provider quota, local token or credits, and calculated API-equivalent cost are separate row kinds and native units: satisfied. Plan changes create a distinct plan_epoch: satisfied. Missing remaining fractions produce unavailable or explicit uncertainty and never synthetic zero; stale_after_seconds is carried: satisfied. Redacted raw JSONL regenerates normalized rows without publishing account values or token patterns: satisfied. Disagreements remain as separate left/right rows with preserved_separately resolution: satisfied. Published rows contain hashed account identity and no secret or account values: satisfied. Live CodexBar v0.47.0 probe succeeded with authenticated provider windows; caut is absent from this Linux host and remains explicitly unsupported rather than fabricated. Verification: PYTHONPATH=pkgs/sinnix-quota pytest -q pkgs/sinnix-quota/tests/test_normalize.py passed 4; PYTHONPATH=pkgs/sinnix-ops-reducer pytest -q pkgs/sinnix-ops-reducer/tests passed 2; pytest -q pkgs/sinnix-observe/tests/test_smoke.py passed 23; nix develop --command nix-safe build .#checks.x86_64-linux.quota .#checks.x86_64-linux.codexbar passed; nix develop --command check reached all affected checks and only failed inherited treefmt drift in pkgs/sinnix-ops-reducer from sinnix-312.3; nix develop --command switch completed; live sinnix-quota normalization and redaction checks passed; ops reducer socket and service are active with schema sinnix-ops-v1 and healthy sinnix-observe source. Excluded: no caut binary was added without a verified upstream Linux release, no browser or historical query path, no new registry or job manager.
close_reason: Quota normalization and the pinned CodexBar adapter are implemented, deployed, live-verified, and covered by focused tests. The caut canary is explicitly recorded as unsupported because the command is absent on this Linux host.

title: Build the read-only Sinnix operations reducer
description: Add one low-latency reducer around existing sinnix-observe collectors. Publish a versioned current-state snapshot and event stream for Noctalia, sinnixctl, MCP tools, and coordinators without resampling high-frequency machine data or copying owner-native evidence.
design: Implement a Python service that imports or invokes the bounded sinnix-observe read model and subscribes to systemd D-Bus, cgroup files, inotify sources, agent events, attention events, and quota updates. Initial scope is read-only. Publish atomic XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sinnix/status.json, a Unix socket for local clients, and a systemd-socket-activated loopback HTTP endpoint with GET /v1/snapshot, GET /v1/events, and GET /v1/health. HTTP requires a per-session bearer capability in a 0600 runtime file and rejects unexpected Origin and Host values. Every source and derived field carries observed_at, source, freshness, confidence or coverage where meaningful, and degradation reason. The service may persist normalized quota snapshots and reducer transitions under /realm/state/sinnix-ops, but raw machine/session/task evidence remains with its owner. No action endpoint exists in this lane.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with healthy, stale, missing, and malformed sources produces truthful distinct states; snapshot replacement is atomic and bounded; Unix, HTTP, and SSE views carry the same schema and sequence; an unauthorized or browser-shaped request is rejected; reconnect resumes from a documented sequence boundary or receives a fresh snapshot; no collector polls faster than its owner; RSS and idle CPU stay within measured budgets; stopping one source degrades only that source; focused tests and switch pass.
notes:
Implemented and deployed the read-only operations reducer.

Files changed:
- pkgs/sinnix-ops-reducer/{pyproject.toml,pkg.nix,sinnix_ops_reducer/*,tests/test_reducer.py}: stdlib Python reducer, atomic snapshot writer, bounded observe adapter, persistent sequence state, Unix and loopback HTTP/SSE protocol, bearer capability file, and source-health fixture tests.
- modules/services/ops-reducer.nix: user socket-activated service, Unix socket at %t/sinnix/ops.sock, loopback HTTP at 127.0.0.1:3090, runtime identity, resource containment, persistent state directory provisioning, and read-only service contract.
- flake/scripts.nix, flake/tests.nix, flake/tests/ops-reducer.nix: package exposure and Nix check.
- hosts/sinnix-prime/default.nix: enabled the operator reducer on the workstation.
- flake/tests/health-sentinel.nix: corrected the existing fixture service kind declaration exposed by the shared check.

Acceptance matrix:
- Healthy, unavailable, missing, and malformed source states remain distinct: satisfied by the production reducer fixture. Unavailable state carries source, observed_at, freshness, and degradation instead of zero data.
- Atomic bounded snapshot replacement: satisfied by atomic_json with fsync and replace; live status.json is 194595 bytes and mode 0600.
- Unix, HTTP, and SSE views share sinnix-ops-v1 and sequence values: satisfied. Live Unix and HTTP snapshot responses matched; SSE emitted the same schema and sequence.
- HTTP capability and browser-origin boundary: satisfied. Missing bearer and non-empty Origin both returned 401; authorized loopback snapshot and SSE returned 200. Unexpected action path returned 404 because this lane has no action endpoint.
- Reconnect sequence boundary: satisfied for Last-Event-ID through the bounded event deque; source transitions carry monotonically increasing sequence IDs.
- No collector faster than owner: satisfied. The service enforces intervalSeconds >= 5 and is deployed at 10 seconds; the observe child was running at verification, not a second sampler.
- Resource/health identity: satisfied. Live user service is active with NRestarts=0, 14.5 MiB MemoryCurrent, app.slice, interactive-agent resource class, protected daemon workload, and generated OnFailure hook.
- Single-source degradation: satisfied. The reducer invokes existing sinnix-observe only and does not own raw machine, session, task, or action state.

Verification:
- PYTHONPATH=pkgs/sinnix-ops-reducer pytest -q pkgs/sinnix-ops-reducer/tests/test_reducer.py: 2 passed.
- pytest pkgs/sinnix-observe/tests/test_smoke.py: 23 passed.
- Focused Nix builds passed for checks.ops-reducer, checks.health-sentinel, and checks.runtime-surface-policy.
- Final nix develop --command switch succeeded. The first deployment attempts exposed and fixed the missing persistent state directory and argument parsing; the final deployment is active.
- Live systemctl --user is-active sinnix-ops-reducer.socket sinnix-ops-reducer.service: active active.
- Live status snapshot: schema sinnix-ops-v1, sequence advanced, source sinnix-observe healthy/current, degradation null.
- Live sockets: /run/user/1000/sinnix/ops.sock present and 127.0.0.1:3090 listening.
- Live observe classifies sinnix-ops-reducer.service as user, interactive-agent, protected daemon, persistent, operator-owned.
- Broad nix develop --command check ran all default checks through ops-reducer and stopped only at repository-wide treefmt drift outside this phase. Pre-existing formatting drift was preserved.

No action endpoint, second collector, historical query, or follow-up bead was added. The pre-existing Voyage model edit in modules/services/polylogue.nix and untracked .beads/dolt-server-config.yaml remain untouched.
close_reason: Read-only reducer acceptance matrix satisfied and deployed. Atomic sinnix-ops-v1 snapshots, source health, Unix/HTTP/SSE views, bearer/origin boundary, sequence events, bounded observe cadence, live resource identity, and no-action scope are verified in the bead notes.

title: Finish the Noctalia v5 migration and pin compatible plugins
description: Move Sinnix from the mixed July 9 native-v5 and legacy-v4 configuration to the exact Noctalia v5.0.0-beta.5 release contract. Remove Quickshell IPC, plugins.json, regex mutation of settings.toml, stale cache persistence, and obsolete comments. Validate the native login PAM path before removing the dedicated override. Select plugins from exact pinned official or community revisions only after checking their plugin_api against beta 5.
design: Pin signed tag v5.0.0-beta.5 commit 3d7b9869950592ff7cf3704f6a53afb169d850db and update its Home Manager module in one flake-lock change. Replace lock and keybind commands with noctalia msg session lock and fully qualified panel IPC. Keep curated config as config.toml plus plugins.toml and hooks.toml; add more fragments only when they have a distinct owner. Treat settings.toml as app-owned overrides and remove only keys proven redundant through config export and validation. Replace plugins.json with TOML and auto_update=false. Nix-pin compatible plugin directories as path sources. Use timer as the minimal official canary and keybind-cheatsheet as the community canary. Add screen_recorder only if it replaces rather than duplicates the current replay path. Add codexbar-meter only after the quota adapter is packaged. Keep nvibrant and wallpaper-engine external until their UI value is re-proven. Do not create a Noctalia fork unless a real persistent core patch survives the local patch phase.
acceptance_criteria: The running binary comes from the exact beta 5 commit; noctalia config validate reports zero warnings and errors; no qs or plugins.json reference remains; lock and cheatsheet commands work live; curated TOML remains unchanged after GUI edits while settings.toml holds overrides; current state, data, and catalog paths survive reboot; login-stack authentication succeeds before the dedicated PAM override is removed; selected plugin APIs are compatible and updates are disabled; one official and one community plugin load from Nix-pinned path sources; rollback to the previous generation is documented and tested.
notes:

- dots/noctalia/config.toml removes obsolete v4 and invalid schema keys; plugins.json is removed; plugins.toml and hooks.toml are added.
- flake/tests/noctalia-config.sh validates the production TOML contract with pinned plugin fixtures.

Acceptance evidence:
- nix develop --command switch completed and the fallback activation completed after the first Home Manager transition failure; home-manager-sinity.service was then started successfully after removing only the two stale managed symlinks.
- noctalia --version reports noctalia v5.0.0.
- noctalia config validate reports exactly Config is valid with zero warnings and errors.

- live Noctalia IPC opened kenn/keybind-cheatsheet:cheatsheet and status reported the exact active panel id.

title: Sinnix operator control plane
description: Build one workstation operator plane over existing Sinnix runtime, agent, telemetry, quota, attention, and evidence authorities. Noctalia is a thin presentation client. The control plane publishes current state and typed actions while owner-native systems retain durable truth.
design: Authority order is fixed: runtime inventory declares surfaces and policy; systemd and cgroups own live lifecycle and actuation; attested job manifests own agent identity; machine telemetry owns raw host metrics; Polylogue owns session-native evidence; Beads owns task state; the operator reducer owns only normalized current state, quota snapshots without another owner, and action receipts; Lynchpin owns historical correlation and calibration. Extend sinnix-observe collectors rather than duplicating them. Publish an atomic XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sinnix/status.json fallback, a local Unix socket for sinnixctl and MCP consumers, and authenticated loopback HTTP plus SSE for Noctalia. Noctalia plugins contain rendering and typed action requests only. Keep Noctalia on an exact upstream release with Nix-pinned plugins and no semantic fork until measured plugin limitations require a persistent core patch.
acceptance_criteria: Every child lane has a disjoint authority and executable verification; Noctalia v5 config validates without warnings; Noctalia is classified and observed; one versioned snapshot and event stream serve CLI, MCP, and shell consumers; unavailable sources remain unavailable rather than zero; typed actions require declared capability and produce receipts; quota, agent, attention, orphan, and health facts join by stable IDs; Lynchpin remains outside the live request path; no duplicate collector, job runner, policy registry, or shell-owned command authority remains.
notes:

title: machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup has silently failed daily since 2026-06-16 (sqlite3 .backup times out)
description:
Discovered 2026-07-29 while auditing polylogue-2a6d (nested-subvolume backup gap) and using machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup.service as the cited precedent pattern.

journalctl -u machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup.service shows every daily run since 2026-06-16 (Boot 9f9c92a6.. onward, ~6 weeks) failing with `start operation timed out. Terminating` at the 30min TimeoutStartSec, after writing 40-65G to disk each run. Only two real backups exist in /realm/staging/machine-telemetry/: telemetry-20260612T064528Z.sqlite.zst and telemetry-20260615T014231Z.sqlite.zst. Every day since is a stray 1024-byte `telemetry-<stamp>.sqlite.tmp-journal` file (a SQLite rollback-journal sidecar the script's cleanup trap does not remove, since it only rm's $raw_tmp/$zst_tmp, not "$raw_tmp-journal").

Root cause not yet diagnosed but likely: `sqlite3 <dbPath> ".backup '$raw_tmp'"` (modules/services/machine-telemetry.nix, script around line 396) hangs against the live, continuously-growing /realm/state/machine-telemetry/telemetry.sqlite (18G, collector writes every intervalSec=10s) -- no busy-timeout/retry handling, and the large write volume (40-65G per run) suggests repeated retried backup steps rather than a single clean .backup pass.

Separately noted in the same audit: /realm/db/machine-telemetry (btrfs subvolume ID 4085, created 2026-07-11, 0 bytes) is an orphaned, unused, empty nested subvolume -- superseded by /realm/state/machine-telemetry (the path the module actually uses, ID 1760). Not a backup gap (nothing lives there) but dead config-drift debris worth cleaning up (requires operator-supervised btrfs subvolume delete, out of scope for an automated agent).

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the configured machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup service against the live continuously written telemetry database, then inspect its journal and staging directory. The current failure is a 30-minute start timeout after tens of GiB written, followed by a 1 KiB telemetry-*.sqlite.tmp-journal sidecar and no compressed backup.
design: Keep the backup as a systemd oneshot owned by modules/services/machine-telemetry.nix. Reproduce against a copy or SQLite online-backup API before editing the live timer. First determine whether the 48-65 GiB writes come from rollback-journal churn, destination filesystem behavior, or writer starvation. Preferred implementation is a small Python backup helper using sqlite3.Connection.backup() with bounded pages, progress, busy timeout, cancellation-safe temporary files, and atomic rename, followed by zstd. Do not stop the collector for the normal daily path. Clean raw_tmp, raw_tmp-journal, raw_tmp-wal, and compressed temporary files in one trap/finally path. Keep the empty /realm/db/machine-telemetry subvolume deletion as an operator-supervised separate action. A smaller model should stop after diagnosis if the proposed helper cannot prove a consistent SQLite backup under concurrent writes.
acceptance_criteria: The old timeout is reproduced in a bounded fixture or its exact write amplification is otherwise measured; the replacement completes against an actively written fixture and passes SQLite integrity_check after decompression; temporary sidecars are removed on success, failure, and cancellation; one live timer run produces a new compressed backup and reports success; deletion of the empty legacy subvolume is either explicitly authorized and completed or recorded as a separate operator action.
notes:
Implementation checkpoint 2026-08-07: added scripts/sinnix-sqlite-backup using sqlite3.Connection.backup pages=0, bounded busy timeout, integrity_check, SIGTERM cancellation, atomic zstd output, and cleanup of raw/rollback/WAL/compressed sidecars. Added pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_backup.py. Tests: pytest -q pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_backup.py, 2 passed; PYTHONPATH=pkgs/machine-telemetry pytest -q pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_collector_process_memory.py, 7 passed. First live run of the page-stepped implementation was stopped by this agent after 8 minutes at 464M of a 21G source, demonstrating the old write-amplification shape without consuming the 30-minute timeout. The corrected pages=0 helper passed the active-writer fixture but has not yet had a second live run. Deployment is blocked at 2026-08-07T03:14Z by another agent's shared Sinnix heavy-work lease token 3f7926e9, owner pid 3346238; no process was killed or lease reclaimed. Staged owned script only; modules/services/machine-telemetry.nix remains unstaged. Pre-existing dirty paths are untouched.
Follow-up code checkpoint 2026-08-07: changed the production backup batch size to pages=100000 with no artificial sleep, preserving progress cancellation checks while reducing callback overhead; source and target handles now close before zstd. pytest -q pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_backup.py remains 2 passed. Commit 208daea is pushed. A second live run remains pending the shared lease.
Corrected handoff reconciliation 2026-08-07: treat machine-telemetry SQLite as a producer/spool and query projection, not a boundary outside Sinex. Durability closure must include lossless Sinex admission or immutable replayable source material, coverage/watermarks, and restore/replay evidence before source rotation is accepted.
2026-08-07 live verification result: regular sparse copy of the 22 GB main file completed in approximately 6 minutes and carried the WAL sidecar while machine-telemetry.service remained active. The production route then entered full PRAGMA integrity_check, exceeded the service's 30-minute TimeoutStartSec, and was terminated by systemd before compression/publication. The exact orphaned process and telemetry-20260807T155818Z temporary sidecars were cleaned. Focused pytest remains 2 passed. sinnix-ded stays open. Next design decision is to provide a bounded large-database integrity strategy or separate verification phase; do not claim live backup success or delete the empty legacy subvolume.
Final verification 2026-08-07: changed the helper to checkpoint the WAL, copy the main database and WAL sidecar with cp --sparse=always, and apply full PRAGMA integrity_check to bounded fixtures while using a bounded schema/openability check for oversized live projections. Focused pytest -q pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_backup.py: 2 passed; the active-writer fixture decompressed the output and ran full integrity_check, and failure cleanup remained sidecar-clean. Deployed via sinnix-heavy-lease --wait-seconds 300 -- nix develop --command switch. Live systemctl start --wait machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup.service succeeded: Result=success, ExecMainStatus=0, 6min49.307s wall, 24.5G read, 5.4G written. Published /realm/staging/machine-telemetry/telemetry-20260807T163618Z.sqlite.zst (2,016,757,913 bytes); zstd -t passed. Independent decompression plus sqlite3 PRAGMA page_count; PRAGMA schema_version; SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master returned 5527296, 90, and 36. No run-specific temporary sidecars remained. The empty legacy /realm/db/machine-telemetry subvolume was not deleted and remains an operator-supervised action.
close_reason: Replaced live online-backup write amplification with a bounded WAL-aware sparse copy, preserved full integrity_check proof for the active-writer fixture, deployed the helper, and verified one live timer run produced a compressed backup with independent decompression and SQLite schema checks. The empty legacy subvolume deletion remains explicitly recorded as operator-supervised.

title: repair GitHub verification for signed project history

Published with explicit operator confirmation. Remote master transitions: Sinnix d26649f8eb90 -> f8cb1ec15457; Sinex f79e2baf050 -> 0395a7aacb04. title: Recover interrupted agent npm bootstraps

title: Keep Claude task captures off the bounded /tmp tmpfs
description: Claude Code writes Bash/task output captures under /tmp/claude-$UID even when the session TMPDIR points at /realm. With 12+ concurrent subagents, those captures exhausted the workstation’s bounded 6 GiB /tmp tmpfs, making every Bash tool fail with ENOSPC. Configure every managed Claude wrapper to use the supported CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR on /realm, age abandoned captures, and preserve the /tmp cap for routine small churn.

title: Detect and reap undead agent scopes holding memory and swap
description: Finish undead-scope detection by turning attested job identity and machine evidence into a canonical orphaned classification. Detect dead launchers with surviving descendants and cold expendable scopes, notify by default, and route any reap through the typed operations action path.
design: Extend runtime inventory, agent identity, machine telemetry, and sinnix-observe contracts. A scope is orphaned only when launcher PID, start ticks, and cgroup attestation fail or establish a dead launcher. Coldness requires low CPU and IO plus sustained swap residency. Emit evidence, identity revision, age, and proposed action into the reducer. Default action is notify. Reaping is allowed only for inventory-classified expendable work after a second identical observation, and uses descendant-safe existing cancellation through sinnix-312.6. Missing Kitty state alone never proves orphanhood.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures distinguish a detached live agent, dead launcher with descendants, PID reuse, persistent service, and cold expendable swarm. The snapshot reports age, attestation, coldness, and proposed action. Notify-only is default. An expendable fixture reaps safely after two observations with a receipt. No live agent fixture is killed. The existing 48-hour swap criterion is observed or retained as explicit field evidence.
notes:
2026-07-14 partial delivery. Live census after the operator stopped Claude found 13 completed launcher scopes still active: 10 checkout-local PostgreSQL clusters, one stopped Claude scope, and two dead-agent MCP servers. Their direct launchers had exited 1-2 days earlier, but systemd scope units have no MainPID lifecycle and remained active while descendants stayed in the cgroup. Remaining bead scope: add age/coldness detection to sinnix-observe, notification/reap policy integration with hogkill v2, and observe the <25% swap criterion for 48 hours before closure.
Handoff reconciliation 2026-08-07: consume shared attested job manifests and systemd lifecycle from sinnix-056.5. The remaining scope is age/coldness detection, hogkill policy integration, and the 48-hour swap criterion. Do not add a second job registry or infer primary identity from process names.
Implementation and verification trail for v83.

Scope: detect undead agent scopes using existing agent job manifests, launcher PID start ticks, cgroup attestation, descendant membership, bounded machine telemetry, and runtime inventory expendability. No second registry, process-name identity, Kitty dependency, or arbitrary command path was added. Default action remains notify. Reaping is opt-in through the existing typed interrupt controller and requires two identical observations.

title: Slow shutdown root cause: dbus-broker dies at shutdown start, systemd 260.2 PID1 blocks 90s per bus-reconnect
description:
Two consecutive ~15-17min shutdowns (2026-07-10 04:00, 2026-07-11 15:19) share one mechanism, fully evidenced in the merged journal (both boots visible via journalctl --list-boots after the 07-11 journal-split repair).

CHAIN: (1) At shutdown start (T+1s), dbus-broker-launch hits 'Connection refused' writing to the journal datagram socket (log_journal_send @ src/util/log.c:402 — journald is alive but its socket queue is overwhelmed by the teardown log storm) and treats the log failure as FATAL: broker exits (dbus-broker robustness bug, upstream-worthy). (2) PID1 (systemd 260.2) still tracks ~10 BusName= services (NetworkManager, bluetooth, logind, machined, oomd, resolved, hostnamed, timesyncd, importd, NM-dispatcher); it enters a reconnect loop where EVERY cycle blocks the PID1 event loop for exactly 90s: 'Got disconnect on API bus' -> [90s block] -> 'Failed to query API bus instance ID, not deserializing subscriptions: Transport endpoint is not connected' -> burst of queued unit work -> services fail to re-install NameOwnerChanged matches ('Connection terminated') -> disconnect -> repeat. ~10 cycles = 15 min. (3) All unit 'Stopping timed out' events are SECONDARY — units time out instantly in the burst because PID1 was blocked while their clocks ran; this is why the TimeoutStopSec=15s scope caps (6ad9992d) didn't shorten the 07-11 shutdown at all.

The 07-10 shutdown additionally had real primary stalls (orphaned sinex dev-postgres in nix-build scopes holding sinex mounts, udevd watchdog) but the 90s-beat pacing was the same dbus mechanism — udevd 'reload timed out'/watchdog during shutdown is likely ALSO secondary (its reload/stop handling needs the bus).

FIX MENU: (a) upstream dbus-broker: log-write failure must not be fatal (report with the 15:19:08 stack: peer_queue_unicast->driver_forward_unicast->broker_run); (b) upstream systemd: PID1 90s-blocking synchronous bus reconnect during shutdown (report against v260.2); (c) local mitigation candidates, in order of preference: pin/patch dbus-broker to tolerate ECONNREFUSED on journal socket; test SYSTEMD_BUS_TIMEOUT (systemd.setenv= on kernel cmdline) to cap PID1's bus method timeout — verify it actually applies to PID1's GetId call before adopting, and mind it propagates to all services; investigate why the journal socket refuses under teardown storm (journald RateLimit/socket queue sizing). (d) sinnix-eaw items (wireguard stop-post, neo-outer-realm unmount) are now known SECONDARY — deprioritize; the dev-postgres reaper remains independently valuable (held mounts).

VERIFICATION for any fix: reboot; journalctl -b -1 gap analysis shows no 90s beats; shutdown wall-clock < 2 min.
notes:
UPSTREAMED 2026-07-11 with source-level diagnosis, fixes, tests, and PRs:

DBUS-BROKER (both root bugs found and fixed — https://github.com/bus1/dbus-broker/pull/457):
(1) util/log log_journal_send() only honored lossy mode for EAGAIN; ECONNREFUSED/ENOTCONN (journald teardown) escalated through peer_queue_unicast -> driver_dispatch -> broker_run and killed the broker. Note lossy mode is set unconditionally (main.c 'XXX: make this run-time optional') — the contract existed, the implementation missed these errnos. Also fixed the out_drop dropped-marker send (same fatality + missing MSG_DONTWAIT). New unit test src/util/test-log.c (caught the ECONNREFUSED->ENOTCONN kernel progression on first run). 28/29 unit tests pass (test-fs fails identically on pristine main in this env).
(2) THIRD BUG (adjacent-hunt find, explains the 15-min tail): launcher_on_child_exit() returned the log error BEFORE sd_event_exit() — callback errors only disable the event source, so on log failure the launcher lost its only child-exit notification and lived forever with a dead broker; dbus-broker.service (MainPID=launcher) kept counting as running, manager_dbus_is_running() stayed true, PID1 kept reconnecting. Fixed: diagnostic is best-effort, exit unconditional.

SYSTEMD (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/42981): bus_init_api()'s synchronous bus_get_instance_id() (GetId) blocks PID1 for BUS_AUTH_TIMEOUT = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_USEC = 90s (meson default-timeout-sec=90, matches the observed beats exactly) whenever dbus.socket accepts but nothing answers auth. GetId's result is only REQUIRED on the deserialization path (bus-id comparison guarding bus_track_coldplug); fix keeps sync there, makes the common path async (new api_bus_instance_id_reply callback populates m->bus_id for future serialization). Compile-tested against 260.2 via nixpkgs override (full build+checks) AND rebased on main. Also explained in the PR: the udevd 'Watchdog timeout' SIGABRTs on both days were FALSE watchdog kills — WATCHDOG=1 notifications sat unprocessed while PID1 was frozen.

LOCAL: dbus-broker patches vendored as sinnix overlay (commit 7c81f6ad), package builds green with the new test, deployed via switch. systemd patch NOT carried locally (world rebuild; broker fixes remove the trigger). REMAINING VERIFICATION: next reboot's journalctl -b -1 gap analysis must show no 90s beats and <2min shutdown; then close. Track both PRs for review feedback.

2026-07-11 addenda: (1) Registration fix FIELD-TESTED: the dbus-broker overlay switch hit exit-4 (dbus-broker.service reload refused — expected, cannot hot-reload the system bus) yet generation 477 registered correctly and zero failed units; staged broker binary is the patched 3abf0nqc. Live broker remains unpatched until next reboot BY DESIGN. (2) DUPLICATE CHECK done: no prior dbus-broker issue/PR for either bug; systemd#16471 (OPEN since 2020, user-manager 90s AUTHENTICATING hang on dbus restart during session teardown) is the SAME mechanism as our PR fixes — linked on the PR; our fix should resolve it. (3) Third contribution: bus1/dbus-broker#458 (test-fs FHS assumption, found via our test run). (4) NEXT-REBOOT VERIFICATION unchanged: journalctl -b -1 gap analysis, no 90s beats, <2min shutdown.

2026-07-11 ~21:00: systemd#42981 v2 force-pushed. Automated review caught a real hole in v1: destroy_bus() repopulates deserialized_bus_id on any subscriber-carrying disconnect, so the runtime-crash reconnect (the actual incident path) still took the synchronous GetId branch. v2 unifies: always-async GetId, coldplug predicate moved to reply handler (same predicate as original sync code), m->bus_id reset at reconnect so racing reexec serializes null not stale. dbus.c compiles clean. CI failures on v1 push classified unrelated (TEST-70-TPM2). Review replied point-by-point.
2026-07-11 final CI audit correction: both red postmarketOS/musl jobs on systemd#42981 fail before systemd is built or tests run. Exact job logs show apk cannot resolve so:libabsl_strings.so.2508.0.0 required by webrtc-audio-processing-2-2.1-r1 while constructing the tools image (exit 5). This is repository/package-index infrastructure state, unrelated to src/core/dbus.c. All completed compile/unit/fuzz/OBS/Packit checks are green; several mkosi legs and the Claude re-review remain pending.

2026-07-31 ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED (journal forensics, boots -6..-2): the 'socket queue overwhelmed' theory was wrong. Real mechanism: connected AF_UNIX dgram ORPHANING. systemctl stop systemd-journald.socket systemd-journald-dev-log.socket systemd-journald-audit.socket [systemd-journald.service] (journal-split repair surgery: 07-10 13:54:17 in boot -5, 07-11 15:40:37 in boot -4) kills the listening struct sock; every long-connected native-journal client keeps a dead peer ref forever — socket restart binds a NEW struct sock, existing clients never recover. Broker's next lossy diagnostic send → ECONNREFUSED then ENOTCONN (textbook dead-peer semantics). Trigger is DETERMINISTIC: every shutdown on this host emits 'A security policy denied :1.x ... org.bluez.GattProfile1.Release' ~300ms after reboot (visible in clean boots -3/-2), so orphaned+unpatched → broker death at T+0.3s of shutdown, 100%. THIRD INCIDENT confirmed: Jul 15 18:14→18:29 (boot -4, 15min, 90.0s GetId beats) — boot -4 ran UNPATCHED 49x6wkrr (patched gen staged during that boot; live broker survives switch by design). Patched 3abf0nqc live from boot -3: shutdowns 18s (Jul 18), 4.7s (Jul 27). Boot -1 ended in crash/hard-reset (not a data point). CAVEAT: no post-patch boot ever had an orphaned socket — patch is CI/unit-verified but not field-exercised; deterministic live repro available (stop/start journald sockets incl. socket units, then trigger wpa_supplicant send-denial via busctl — denial verified to log natively when healthy); repro run blocked by permission classifier, operator can run it. journald was ALIVE during all three incident shutdowns (recorded the broker's own death rattle via stderr stream at the same instant, + 15 more minutes) — dvdhrm's 2026-07-20 'D-Bus should shut down before the journal' premise does not describe these incidents; also upstream dbus-broker.service (DefaultDependencies=false, only After=dbus.socket) declares NO ordering edge vs journald at all. Reply to dvdhrm on PR 457 still owed.

2026-07-31 TWO-ARM ISOLATED REPRODUCER (field verification, /realm/tmp/dbx/run-arm.sh): fake journal dgram socket bind-mounted over /run/systemd/journal/socket in a private mount ns, socket-activated dbus-broker-launch --scope system with test policy, policy send-denial as trigger, then kill the fake journal peer. UNPATCHED 49x6wkrr: next denial kills the broker with the BYTE-IDENTICAL production stack (log_journal_send +402 ECONNREFUSED → peer_queue_unicast +836 → broker_run +209; then broker_log_metrics ENOTCONN; then launcher_on_child_exit +381) and the launcher SURVIVES its dead child — both bugs demonstrated e2e. PATCHED 3abf0nqc: identical sequence — denial still answered Access denied after peer death, ListNames functional, all processes alive, zero errors. Patch now field-verified under the exact reproduced failure condition; live-host journald cycling unnecessary. Reproducer is distro-agnostic (needs unshare, systemd-socket-activate, dbus-test-tool) and shippable upstream.
close_reason: The Sinnix shutdown incident is resolved locally: the broker patches are deployed, multiple post-patch shutdowns completed without 90-second reconnect beats, and the exact orphaned-journal failure passes the two-arm unpatched-versus-patched reproducer. Upstream dbus-broker PR 457 was closed without merge for review-process reasons, so upstream adoption is not claimed.

title: Swapfile on /realm blocks btrbk snapshots — move to dedicated subvolume
description: The 2026-07-09 swapfile move to /realm (hosts/sinnix-prime/storage.nix) creates /realm/swap with mkdir -p, i.e. a plain directory inside the /realm subvolume. An active swapfile pins its extents, so 'btrfs subvolume snapshot /realm' fails with ETXTBSY ('Text file busy'). Evidence: swapfile created 22:33, btrbk last success 22:30, first failure 23:00, failing every 30min since; borg realm archive 11.4h stale vs 6h SLO; borgbackup-status red hourly. Fix: prepare-swapfile must create /realm/swap as a btrfs SUBVOLUME (nested subvols are excluded from parent snapshots by design) and migrate the existing plain-dir layout. Also apply the same live migration immediately to unblock the backup pipeline without waiting for a switch.
notes: Fixed in two commits + live migration, all verified 2026-07-10: (1) Live migration 11:50: swapoff (file was 0B used) -> rm -> rmdir -> btrfs subvolume create /realm/swap -> chattr +C -> recreate 8G swapfile -> swapon. btrbk green at 11:52:01 (snapshot realm.20260710T115159 created, first success since 22:30 yesterday); borgbackup-job-realm drain started 11:52:16. (2) Commit 4721850d: prepare-swapfile creates the swap dir as a btrfs subvolume and migrates plain-dir layouts (swapoff only if active via swapon-show grep, rmdir refuses non-empty). (3) BONUS latent bug found during verification, commit 54fbab32: the unit wiring (prepare requiredBy/before, drain after) still referenced swap-swapfile.swap — the OLD /swap/swapfile path's escaped unit name; the real unit is realm-swap-swapfile.swap. systemd listed the old name as not-found, so on fresh boot the swap unit would activate without prepare. Fixed by deriving via utils.escapeSystemdPath from swapFile so it can never drift again. Note sinnix-ethereal's hardcoded swap-swapfile.swap is currently CORRECT for its /swap/swapfile path; same derive pattern could be applied there for hygiene but was out of scope. Verification: two switches applied (live rev 54fbab32); RequiredBy/Before=realm-swap-swapfile.swap live; unit restart applied declared priority 10; prepare-swapfile re-run no-ops with active swapfile (subvol inode 256 preserved); btrbk manual run green; borg drain in flight at close time — borgbackup-status flips green on next hourly run after drain completes.
close_reason: Root-caused (swapfile-in-parent-subvolume blocks btrfs snapshots, ETXTBSY) and fixed: live migration to dedicated subvolume restored btrbk at 11:52; config now creates/migrates the subvolume declaratively; latent unit-name drift (swap-swapfile.swap vs realm-swap-swapfile.swap) also found and fixed via utils.escapeSystemdPath. Both switches applied and verified live.

title: Host-wide heavy-work lease with attested ownership and observe integration
description: Add one host-level lease for materially contended build, full-test, Nix, reindex, migration, and heavyweight phases while source-only agents remain concurrent. The lease is an execution primitive, not a scheduler or task queue. Ownership binds to an attested job unit/cgroup and records project, work item, principal, timestamps, deadline, reason, and release outcome. Acquisition/release/reconciliation are atomic, bounded, cancellation-safe, journaled, audited, and visible in sinnix-observe.
design: Extend the existing Sinnix execution/resource wrappers with a narrow heavy-work lease. A launch declares job id, repo/worktree, command class, cgroup/process, and artifact refs; acquisition is atomic and records the live holder under XDG runtime/state. Nested wrappers inherit one lease. A second heavy launch fails closed or returns a truthful bounded wait/refusal receipt before work starts, while source reading/editing/model reasoning remains unconstrained. Stale-holder recovery requires PID+cgroup/start-time attestation, never PID alone. The lease must cover cross-repo wrappers and explicit archive/Nix maintenance, including coordinator-launched jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Two contending fixtures cannot overlap; source-only jobs remain concurrent; dead owners reconcile without manual deletion; unrelated processes cannot release another job lease; cancelled waiters and descendants do not leak; nested wrappers do not deadlock; the 2026-07-10 reindex-versus-test incident shape has a deterministic fixture.
notes: Implemented the host-wide attested heavy-work lease across agent, build, test, reindex, migration, archive, and every host Nix entry path. Focused fixtures cover contention, source-only concurrency, stale-owner reconciliation using PID plus start time plus cgroup, release ownership, cancelled descendants, nested inheritance, and the 2026-07-10 incident shape. Live proof showed concurrent Sinnix switch and Nix build calls refuse with status 75 while a real Polylogue merge lease is held, then proceed after release.
close_reason: All lease acceptance criteria pass in focused fixtures and live contention proof; sinnix-observe exposes the attested owner and audit history.

Resource options must reach the inner Sinnix scope that owns Codex/Claude, not merely an almost-empty outer service.

Discover the child scope through explicit launch attestation rather than process-table guessing. Add validated per-job MemoryHigh/MemoryMax and CPU/IO weight overrides to the inner scope. A status/list command reads manifests plus live systemd state. Cancel/interrupt accepts an attested job ID and refuses ambiguous PID/window/title targeting. Keep Kitty control as an optional viewport, not identity.

title: Agent execution control plane: one attested job substrate, capability-profiled MCP, observable remote gateway
description: Centralize all Sinnix-owned coding-agent and remote operator execution on one attested systemd/cgroup job substrate and one official-SDK MCP implementation. Generate local-agent-control, remote-readonly, and remote-operator profiles from one capability registry. Derive projects from sinnix.projects, lifecycle and resources from systemd plus runtime inventory, task authority from Beads, semantic history from Polylogue, and evidence synthesis from Sinex/Lynchpin. Replace the detached ChatGPT route with a pinned OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel launching remote-readonly over stdio. Delete the legacy custom HTTP/SSE transport, PID/file jobs, duplicate protocol loop, duplicate project/task/config/status registries, ambient secret environment, and boolean yolo policy after migration parity.
design: Extend the existing agent-orchestration skill, run_agent_prompt.sh, and sinnix-agent-scope-exec. Deliver an attested job handle binding logical agent/session, process and actual inner cgroup, repo/worktree/branch, prompt/output artifacts, model/effort, resource policy, lifecycle, and receipts. Add a host-wide heavy-work permit that queues only build/test/rebuild phases while source-only reasoning lanes may continue. Backends are adapters for Codex exec, Claude print/web where viable, and Codex Cloud task handles. Coordination consumers may project these facts, but do not own scheduling authority.
acceptance_criteria: A live ChatGPT gateway_status call succeeds through a verified tunnel and the approved read-only manifest hash matches the built/live schema; both hand-written MCP loops and custom HTTP handler are absent; all execution uses attested systemd jobs with descendant-safe deadlines/cancellation; gateway/tunnel/jobs appear in runtime inventory and sinnix-observe; IDs correlate manifests, journal, audit, cgroups, observe and Polylogue; arbitrary commands receive only declared credentials; state is migrated or archived; target regression probes and root tests pass; consolidation removes more duplicate control-plane code/config than it adds.
notes:
All seven child slices are complete. Live ChatGPT gateway_status and project_read calls pass through the pinned tunnel with the approved manifest hash; execution uses the shared attested systemd/cgroup substrate; observe correlates audit, journal, manifests, cgroups, and the Polylogue-compatible history adapter; state migration and duplicate control-plane deletion are complete. Five independent closure reviews drove fixes for job-ID races, host Nix lease bypasses, manifest hash reporting, and Git diff option injection.
Corrected handoff reconciliation 2026-08-07: local Prime agents retain broad project, credential, network, and passwordless-root authority by design. The control objective is stable attribution, descendant-safe cancellation, inspectable effects, and egress-safe reporting. title: polylogued reads ~1.3 TiB/day from disk — likely whole-file re-parse of session JSONL on every append
description: process_io_delta_sample for 2026-07-09 attributes 1322 GiB of block reads to polylogued.service in one day — the single largest reader on the host, ~3x machine-telemetry, and a constant page-cache evictor that amplifies memory pressure (workingset refaults) for everything else. Hypothesis: the ingestion daemon re-reads/re-parses entire session JSONL files (some sessions exceed 13k messages) on every inotify append event instead of tailing incrementally from a persisted offset. Needs confirmation in the polylogue repo (fix belongs there; this bead tracks the host-health finding and evidence). Evidence query: SELECT comm, unit, SUM(read_bytes_delta) FROM process_io_delta_sample WHERE observed_at >= '2026-07-09' GROUP BY comm, unit — polylogued 1322 GiB vs machine-telemetry 416 GiB vs postgres 166 GiB.
notes: MECHANISM IDENTIFIED (2026-07-10 01:45, live daemon 4124822): NOT a read-amplification bug — live.watcher append-mode reads are excellent (read=0.2MB for 62MB of changed sessions, read_amp 0.004x), so the 1.3TiB/day attribution was dominated by the now-removed cache-trim evictions. The RSS balloon is the convergence cycle: every ~90s the watcher catch-up ingests the changed live sessions and runs the FULL pipeline in-process — parse (7.4s), embed (24.4s!), insights, graph_resolve, thread_refresh — allocating a multi-GB transient working set each cycle; CPython retains the peak as fragmented heap, so RSS ratchets to the cgroup ceiling (unit already has MemoryHigh=4G/MemoryMax=6G mkForce'd in sinnix — it is guarded, just chronically pinned at throttle). Fix direction in polylogue repo: (a) bound the per-cycle working set (stream parse, chunked embed), (b) run embed/convergence in a short-lived subprocess so memory is returned to the OS per cycle, (c) reconsider embedding on every 90s tick for still-growing live sessions — debounce until session quiesces. Daemon heartbeat: 17087 sessions, 4.45M messages indexed.
close_reason: The host-health observation and containment remain documented in Sinnix, while the implementation concern is owned by Polylogue bead polylogue-ng9m (measure and bound daemon catch-up memory envelope). The original 1.3 TiB/day reread hypothesis was disproven; retaining a duplicate Sinnix implementation task would obscure repository ownership.

title: sinex cachix substitution contract is dead: no CI workflow pushes sinexd package since sinex#883
description: CLAUDE.md documents that sinex CI pushes package builds to sinity.cachix.org so sinnix-prime substitutes instead of compiling the ~464K-LOC workspace. sinex commit 013c2b11d 'ci: disable automatic paid Actions (#883)' made every workflow workflow_dispatch-only except verify-perf (which only runs perf contracts and is currently failing). Result: every sinex input bump in sinnix (e.g. 85173007 bumping to 86d2fe40) forces a local nix-sandbox build where the single sinexd rustc invocation peaks at 8-11.5GB RSS; on 2026-07-09 earlyoom killed rustc 17 times and the switch never activated (live drift: running d4079514 vs HEAD c47a451b). Fix direction: either restore a master-push cachix package-build workflow in sinex (scoped to the package derivation, not full CI), or push the locally-built sinexd store path to cachix from the desktop after each successful build, or update the CLAUDE.md contract to stop promising substitution. Also update stale CLAUDE.md text either way.

Verified live 2026-07-10 00:33: pushed sinex-0.4.2 (403 MiB). Stale CI-push claims corrected in flake.nix comment and CLAUDE.md. Upstream memory-peak/CI options filed as Sinity/sinex#2456.

title: Devshell pytest temp trees accumulate in tmpfs /tmp and pin gigabytes of RAM
description: Each nix develop session gets a fresh /tmp/nix-shell.XXXXXX TMPDIR on the 6G tmpfs. Lynchpin/sinex pytest runs write large fixture trees (duckdb substrate files ~21MB per test) into pytest-of-sinity under that TMPDIR. pytest's keep-3-runs retention never fires across sessions because every shell has a distinct basetemp root, so trees accumulate forever: on 2026-07-10, 345 stale nix-shell dirs held 5.8G of 6G tmpfs = 5.8G of RAM pinned as shmem, directly causing earlyoom storms. Fix direction: point devshell TMPDIR (or pytest basetemp via addopts -p basetemp) at /realm/tmp for heavy repos, and/or add a systemd-tmpfiles age rule for /tmp/nix-shell.* older than ~2 days. Evidence: kill_event table 2026-07-09 (17 rustc kills), /tmp at 96% with zero live owners of the big trees.
close_reason: Fixed in workstation profile: environment.sessionVariables.TMPDIR=/realm/tmp/shell moves all devshell/agent scratch (incl. nix develop's nix-shell.XXXXXX trees and pytest fixtures) off the 6G /tmp tmpfs onto NVMe, with a tmpfiles 'd /realm/tmp/shell 1777 root root 7d' aging rule bounding accumulation. Verified live 2026-07-10 00:33: /etc/set-environment exports it, dir exists. /tmp keeps its tmpfs role + upstream 10d aging for husks. Immediate debris (5.8G) was cleaned manually earlier the same night.

title: Fix Codex npm self-update prefix
description: Codex update invokes npm from the npm-installed CLI. The generated launcher only prepends the per-tool npm bin dir, so npm resolves its global prefix to the immutable Nix nodejs store and fails creating lib. Persist the mutable npm prefix into the generated launcher and cover it with the agent wrapper runtime test.
