title: Social-interaction instrument suite: expression, conversation telemetry, practice loops (autism-support tooling)
description: Operator-personal program (2026-08-11, ultrathink request). Framing principle: instruments for self-knowledge and chosen skill-building, never normalization pressure; personal-baseline statistics over NT-trained classifier judgments; absolutely local (this domain is why the local estate exists). Components: (1) EXPRESSION MIRROR (production side): webcam -> MediaPipe landmarks + OpenFace3/py-feat ACTION UNITS (objective muscle activations — deliberately preferred over contested emotion labels, which mislabel autistic faces) -> 'what does my face broadcast' gauge, live-optional/retrospective-default; practice mode = target-expression prompts scored like vocal GOP. (2) DECODING TRAINER (reading side): flashcard loops from video corpora — pause on face, classify, reveal; VLM (local-multimodal-moe) generates cue EXPLANATIONS (brow/timing/context) not just labels; infinite sarcasm/prosody drills GENERATED via TTS emotion control (same sentence, flipped prosody -> classify intent). (3) CONVERSATION TELEMETRY (strongest piece): the nm7+diarization+parselmouth stack yields objective metrics per conversation — talk-time ratio, interruption/overlap counts, response-latency distribution, monologue-duration histogram, backchannel rate, question rate, prosodic variance (monotone gauge); post-hoc replay-with-metrics via lynchpin; optional MINIMAL live nudges via Noctalia (talk-ratio drift, monologue timer) — default off, cognitive load is the enemy. (4) SPARRING PARTNER: the mke E2E voice loop as unlimited judgment-free conversation practice — personas, difficulty (ambiguity/sarcasm/small-talk), post-session pragmatics critique by local LLM. (5) MASKING-COST TELEMETRY (speculative, data exists): lynchpin-correlate interaction density vs recovery markers (typing cadence, activity, sleep exports) -> evidence-based social budgeting. (6) ALEXITHYMIA SUPPORT (long-horizon): periodic self-reports joined to behavioral capture -> learn personal precursor signatures of overload. Models to grab: OpenFace 3.0 or py-feat (AUs), FER ensemble (secondary), rest already in mke/nm7/w9l programs. Prior art context: affective-computing-for-ASD research exists (expression-training games, MIT-lineage emotion-glasses); nobody ships the telemetry pieces because privacy — local estate is the unlock.
notes:
2026-08-11h refinements: (1) MEDIA-CORRELATION + PERSONAL AFFECT MODEL: watched media (MPRIS/stashbox/browser captures) x facial-AU response x periodic SELF-RATINGS = training data for a personal emotion model — learn the mapping from YOUR AUs+context to YOUR self-reported states, replacing NT-trained classifiers entirely over time. Label frameworks to support: FACS AUs (objective substrate), valence-arousal(-dominance) dimensions (better personal-calibration fit than categories), Ekman categories only as legacy interop, appraisal tags optional. Self-rating capture = lightweight periodic prompts (ties alexithymia component). (2) LLM-CONVERSATION SPECIAL CASE: agent conversations are already fully captured (polylogue) — richest conversational corpus owned; use as (a) low-stakes practice baseline, (b) contrast class vs human conversations (interruption/monologue/latency deltas human-vs-LLM are themselves informative), (c) practice-transfer measurement (does sparring improve human-conversation metrics?). (3) DRILL DESIGN deepened: LLM as item-writer (scenario + intended-intent label) -> TTS emotion rendering -> adaptive difficulty (prosody-only items vs context-conflict items; IRT-style adaptation); VALIDITY fix for TTS-emotion-distribution bias: mine REAL examples from captured/watched media (subtitles+audio+CLAP/AU analysis); prior art anchor: MUStARD multimodal sarcasm dataset (sitcom clips) — both an eval set and a mining pattern. (4) AVATAR-DIRECTOR ARCHITECTURE for sparring: separate director-LLM (maintains explicit hidden character state — goals, emotional state, concealed intent — via CoT/structured state; emits utterance + stage directions incl. TTS emotion params) from actor layer (TTS render); pedagogical gold = post-session REVEAL: your inferences vs the actually-modeled hidden state, turn by turn.
2026-08-11j DIRECTOR-REALISM design (operator insight: is the modeled state actually human-realistic?): use BASE models as the character-statistics engine — post-trained models are mode-collapsed into assistant persona; base models retain the raw human text distribution. Scheme: director samples HIGH-N continuations from a base model conditioned on the scene (what would people actually do/feel here, as a population) -> aggregates into state statistics -> instruct model plays the sampled character. Local base options that fit (none strictly dominated): Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base (MoE, the RAM-offload fit — primary), Qwen2.5-14B/7B base (dense, fast-n sampling), OLMo-2 (fully-open incl. training data — auditability), Llama-3.1-8B-base (legacy ecosystem). NSFW/abliteration note recorded: base models have NO refusal training — abliteration is indeed irrelevant (no refusal direction exists to ablate); they complete anything in-distribution but need conditioning-by-prompt (few-shot) rather than instruction. Closed labs do not serve true base models (no relevant non-open options). Kimi K3 (2026-07-27, 2.8T MoE 104B-active, Modified-MIT): open INSTRUCT weights confirmed; a separate BASE release unconfirmed in coverage — and it is irrelevant locally (104B active far exceeds 32GB RAM offload); K2-Base remains the largest confirmed open base.
2026-08-11k DISTRIBUTION-REALISM caveat (operator's sharp concern): base models learn text-about-behavior, not behavior — domains with strong social-desirability distortion (dating, sexuality) have web-text distributions systematically skewed (performative narratives, advice-column register, erotica tropes vs lived reality); high-n sampling reproduces the NARRATIVE distribution faithfully, which is not the behavior distribution. Mitigations recorded: (a) register triangulation — sample under multiple conditioning frames (candid-anonymous register vs public register) and study the DELTA; (b) OLMo+Dolma to measure what the corpus even contains; (c) treat outputs as distribution-of-stories with explicit uncertainty, never oracle; (d) the frustration is legitimate and unresolvable in principle — no one has ground truth for the gap between overt culture and actual behavior; the tool can at least make the gap VISIBLE by contrasting registers. ALSO: NSFW in pretraining is typically FILTERED (Llama/FineWeb-class corpora classifier-filter adult content; Dolma partially) — base models underrepresent it vs the actual web; another reason OLMo's measurable corpus matters, and a caveat on base-realism for those domains specifically.
2026-08-11 director-mode prior art (ERP community — convergent evolution confirmed): st-stepped-thinking (middleware prompt-chaining: forces generation of character thoughts/emotions/plans BEFORE the reply — our director's deliberation stage, already built as an ST extension pattern), SillyTavern-Tracker + RPG-Companion + MultihogDnDFramework (structured per-turn state: stats/inventory/quests/world progression + RNG systems — proven state-schema shapes to steal), Guided-Generations (operator interjection steering mid-scene), ST-Copilot (OOC meta-assistant/DM-aide channel — the out-of-band control plane). What OUR design still adds beyond their practice: (1) deliberately CONCEALED state with post-hoc pedagogical reveal (their thoughts display immediately; ours hides for the inference-training loop), (2) base-model population sampling for state realism, (3) the voice loop w/ speaker-verified barge-in. Implementation shortcut recorded: prototype the director INSIDE SillyTavern via stepped-thinking + Tracker forks before building bespoke — the middleware hooks exist.
2026-08-11: TALEMATE identified as the closest existing system to the director architecture — open-source RP engine built AS separate agents (director agent, narrator, world-state, memory via vector store) orchestrating the scene, i.e. the community's own agent-separated answer to bare-LLM roleplay; study/steal its agent decomposition before building. Meta context: pure adventure ENGINES (KoboldAI Lite adventure mode, AI-Dungeon-likes) lost to freeform+tracker-extensions because rigid mechanics constrain fiction; the winning shape is LLM narration + mechanical resolution bolted on (dice/state extensions) — the same hybrid our director design already assumes.
2026-08-11 EMERGENT-MECHANICS design (operator idea — better than the engines-vs-freeform dichotomy): the LLM AUTHORS mechanics ongoingly rather than being constrained by prebuilt ones — during play the director proposes/extracts rules ('persuasion here works like X, roll vs rapport'), persists them to a MECHANICS LIBRARY (derived-data shape: rule = {trigger, resolution procedure, dice/threshold, provenance-scene}), and cheap deterministic code + RNG enforces them thereafter (consistency without rigidity; the LLM narrates outcomes it no longer adjudicates alone). Library accumulates across sessions/campaigns = reusable house-rule corpus; rules are re-derivable, versioned, supersedable per the uou derived-data doctrine. This inverts the failed pure-engine model: structure is OUTPUT of play, not input. Prior-art check: AI-Dungeon scripting/Talemate node systems gesture nearby but nothing known does rule-extraction-to-persistent-library; likely novel composition.
2026-08-11 operator clarification on structured-vs-freeform: the interesting third option is the LLM SPINNING ITS OWN MECHANICS ongoingly — improvised formal subsystems (a duel resolution rule, a resource clock, a relationship meter) invented mid-fiction, persisted, reused, and evolved — backed by a MECHANICS LIBRARY the director accumulates across sessions (retrieve-adapt-instantiate, like lorebooks but for RULES). Community trackers gesture at this (MultihogDnD's RNG+lorebook-agent) but nobody does library-accumulating improvised mechanics. Same design shape as kk4's dynamic-grammars idea: dynamically generated formal structure, LLM-managed, persisted as data. Director architecture gains a mechanics-registrar component.
2026-08-11 ATOMIC-SKILL DECOMPOSITION of the social domain (operator ask — the oqa pattern applied here; trainers built on the sinnix-cs9 foundry runtime):
DECODING atomics: (1) micro-expression flash recognition — 30-200ms staircased exposures from the FACS-labeled tiers; (2) incongruence detection — eye-region vs mouth-region emotion mismatch (fake-smile discrimination), trainable by compositing; (3) prosody-meaning atomics: sarcasm/irony detection (TTS-generated + mined real clips per existing MUStARD plan), and STRESS-PLACEMENT semantics ('I didn't say she stole it' x 7 stress positions = 7 meanings — cheap TTS item generation, high leverage for pragmatics); (4) emotional-prosody classification at staircased subtlety.

title: Continuous screen + enriched terminal capture (the remaining senses)
description: Operator wants (2026-08-11): close the non-audio capture gaps. SCREEN: always-on low-rate capture — screenpipe-style frames (0.2-1fps or on-change) + OCR (ties to sinnix-w9l OCR tier) + window/app metadata, NOT full video (4K OLED video is ~2-4GB/hr; frames+OCR+metadata reconstructs almost everything at ~1% the cost). Hyprland event stream ALREADY flows to ops-reducer — join frames to window ids/geometry/workspace from it. TERMINAL: verify asciinema capture is actually operational (census!); enrich casts with correlated hyprland window geometry/position + kitty window identity (kitty-scrollback capture exists) so a session can be recreated as-it-looked: cast + geometry timeline + which display/workspace. Storage: /realm captures conventions, tiered like audio (recent raw, older compressed). Sink: lake + lynchpin correlation.
notes:
READ-TRACKING design (2026-08-11e): streams = webcam gaze region (MediaPipe iris, region-grade) + viewport/scroll (browser via CDP/rrweb from sinnix-ngf; terminals via kitty scrollback position; PDFs via viewer IPC where possible) + screen-OCR word boxes (PaddleOCR-VL frames). Join: dwell-time-weighted paragraph coverage — a paragraph counts as read when it sat in the gazed region for >= personal-reading-speed * its-length (calibrate reading speed from known-read sessions). Output: read-spans JSONL {content-hash, span, confidence, ts} into the lake; lynchpin materializes 'actually-read text' vs 'displayed text' — the delta is itself interesting (skimmed vs studied). Honest granularity: paragraph, not word; confidence field mandatory.
2026-08-11g VIDEO tier added (operator asked possibilities in earnest): gpu-screen-recorder with NVENC HEVC on the 3080 (near-zero CPU) in three modes — (a) REPLAY RING: always-on last-30-min buffer in RAM/realm, save-on-hotkey ('clip that') — the highest-value/lowest-cost video feature; (b) EVENT-TRIGGERED continuous recording (meetings/screenshare detection via PipeWire+portal events); (c) optional continuous 1440p@10-15fps HEVC ~0.5-1.5GB/hr if ever wanted — frames+OCR remains the always-on default, video is the escalation tier. Storage math recorded; DRM/portal caveats apply. ALSO new capture sources approved-for-design: AT-SPI2 accessibility tree (the SEMANTIC screen — roles/labels/text/focus events; complements pixels; needs chromium accessibility flag for Electron/Chrome; GTK good, Qt decent) as focus-follow logger + event stream; D-Bus NOTIFICATION stream (org.freedesktop.Notifications — every notification to the lake); MPRIS media metadata (what played when); live clipboard (clipse exists as export — make continuous); mouse-dynamics telemetry (fatigue/behavior signal, cheap).
2026-08-11h HYBRID SEMANTIC-MASKED VIDEO design (operator idea, recorded as novel — no known shipped system does this): regions covered by semantic capture are EXCLUDED from pixel video and reconstructed at replay: terminals re-render from asciinema casts (deterministic given font/theme — near-pixel-perfect), browser windows re-render via rrweb player (~95% fidelity; canvas/video elements are the honest gaps), hyprland geometry timeline provides exact placement, cursor track via hyprctl cursorpos/libinput polling (cheap, essential). Residual pixel video only for unmasked regions (mpv, games, misc). Feasibility: HIGH terminals / MED-HIGH browser / storage win large; complexity moderate (replay compositor needed for reconstruction). Fallback stance: even without the compositor, capturing everything separately preserves the option.
2026-08-11j ARCHITECTURE UPGRADE (operator direction): per-window capture beats post-hoc masking. Hyprland/wlroots expose hyprland-toplevel-export / wlr-screencopy-class protocols = capture ANY toplevel individually, INCLUDING off-screen and other-workspace windows, damage-driven (frames only when content changes — static windows cost ~zero). New design: per-window encoded streams + geometry/z-order timeline -> ANY view reconstructable (incl. workspaces never displayed); full-screen pixel truth kept only in the 15-30min NVENC ring; archived tier = per-window residual streams with semantically-captured windows (terminals/browser) DROPPED, gaps+wallpaper reconstructed (wallpaper file known to noctalia; hyprland animations acceptable as cheap residual or re-simulated). Record-everything-then-blank fallback: masking to constant color before encode collapses macroblocks to ~nothing — near-full savings without per-window plumbing. SELF-VERIFICATION loop (operator req): periodically render the reconstruction (asciinema/rrweb/wallpaper composite) for a sampled moment and SSIM-compare against the ring-buffer ground truth — capture pipeline that proves its own fidelity, occasionally-continuous as budget allows. Deep-Hyprland data grabs: damage events, animation states, full window-state beyond IPC via plugin API (C++) if the protocols fall short.
2026-08-11 web-recon: (1) landscape re-check — screenpipe is now YC S26 and pivoting to agent-platform ('plug into your agents', OpenClaw/'Hermes agent' integrations); still MIT, Linux build exists; adjacent: ScreenMemory, TimeScroll, Windrecorder, OpenRecall, LUCI (consumer local-recall). Our custom plan stays justified (Wayland/Hyprland-native capture, pixel-perfect semantic masking, lake conventions), but screenpipe's pipeline (capture->OCR->sqlite FTS->API) is the reference implementation to crib from. (2) VIDEO-UNDERSTANDING tier for the archived screen/media video: Qwen3-VL has timestamp-grounded event localization (Text-Timestamp Alignment) — the right shape for 'what happened at minute M' queries over screen video; VideoChat-Flash (ICLR 2026) does ~50x hierarchical token compression with 99.1% needle accuracy on 10K-frame inputs — the archival-scale query architecture. Both open-weight.
2026-08-11 screenpipe DEEP ANALYSIS (fetched README, current): LICENSE FLIPPED — no longer MIT; source-available, personal non-commercial free, commercial paid ($25-150/seat); PostHog telemetry ON by default + Sentry; YC S26, pivoting to teams/agents. Architecture worth stealing: (1) EVENT-DRIVEN capture (app switches, clicks, typing pauses, scroll — not fixed-fps; ~300MB/8h vs ~2GB continuous) — adopt as 9pd's trigger model alongside the periodic baseline; (2) ACCESSIBILITY-TREE-FIRST text extraction with OCR only as fallback (matches our AT-SPI plan; validates the ordering); (3) per-pipe DATA-PERMISSION model (YAML frontmatter: app/window globs, content-type, time windows, endpoint gating, enforced at three layers incl. per-pipe tokens — 'not prompt-based') — the design pattern maps directly onto agent-gateway profile capabilities for capture-data access; (4) storage economics reference: sqlite+FTS5 + JPEG frames, 5-20GB/month. Where our stack wins: capture surfaces already exceed theirs (scribe-tap keylog, atuin, kitty scrollback, ActivityWatch, planned all-channel audio with a better STT tier than their whisper-turbo, sinex event platform, lynchpin cross-source analysis), Linux tier is first-class for us (their Linux = source-build + Tesseract, Wayland unaddressed), lake conventions + replay-later doctrine vs their opaque sqlite, zero telemetry, and semantic masking requirement they don't attempt. Verdict: build 9pd bespoke as planned; import ideas (1)-(3).
2026-08-11 screenpipe-steal mapping onto estate (operator asked): (1) EVENT-DRIVEN TRIGGERS: capture keyed to state-change events (app switch, click burst, typing pause, scroll) instead of fixed-rate polling — this is literally sinex's event-platform doctrine applied to screen capture; implementation: subscribe the 9pd capture daemon to the existing event streams (ActivityWatch window-focus events, scribe-tap activity, Hyprland IPC) — sinex/NATS can BE the trigger bus, giving capture the same replay/provenance properties as every other sinex source. (2) A11Y-FIRST, OCR-FALLBACK: prefer structured text from the accessibility tree (AT-SPI lane already planned in ngf/9pd), OCR only for canvas/games/remote — the estate already practices this principle elsewhere: kitty scrollback capture gets terminal text structured rather than OCRing terminal pixels, polylogue gets session text from JSONL rather than screenshots; screen capture should follow the same 'structured source beats pixels' ordering. (3) PER-PIPE DATA PERMISSIONS: screenpipe grants each agent/pipe declarative scoped access (app/window globs, content types, time windows, endpoint gating, enforced with per-pipe tokens, not prompts) — maps onto agent-gateway capability profiles (remote-readonly/local-agent-control/remote-operator) which currently scope TOOLS; extend the same manifest machinery to scope CAPTURE-DATA queries (which lanes, which time ranges, which apps) when capture surfaces become gateway-queryable. That is the missing design piece for exposing 9pd/nm7 data to agents safely.

title: Faithful web + network capture/archival: DOM-level, WARC traffic, response bodies, video specialcase
description: Operator wants (2026-08-11) rich/faithful/comprehensive web archival, wider network capture to some extent, keep everything, dedup+compress, downstream markdown processing. Design layers: (1) DOM-level session recording via rrweb (the extant project class the operator recalled: records DOM mutations + viewport/scroll/input as replayable JSON — faithful 'how it looked incl. viewport movement' at tiny size) injected via the CDP :9222 infrastructure (polylogue browser-capture receiver already exists as the ingestion path precedent); (2) page snapshots via SingleFile (self-contained HTML) for point-in-time keeps; (3) traffic-level: CDP Network domain response-body capture for browser HTTPS (no MITM needed inside the browser we control!) -> WARC via warcio; browsertrix/pywb class tooling for crawl-shaped archival; (4) LIMITS documented: full-machine HTTPS MITM (mitmproxy+CA) works for browsers but breaks cert-pinned apps and QUIC/HTTP3 (disable h3 or accept gaps) — CDP-side capture sidesteps all of it for the browser, which is most traffic of interest; raw packet capture (pcap) only for metadata/flows, not plaintext; (5) VIDEO: specialcase media URLs via yt-dlp triggered from captured network requests (ytdlp-clip-watch precedent exists). Dedup: content-hash store + WARC revisit records + zstd. Downstream: ReaderLM/Docling -> markdown derivatives, raw kept per lake rules.
notes:
2026-08-11g IN-DEPTH LAYER DESIGN: L0 network metadata — zeek-class conn/dns/tls logs (flows not bodies; QUIC-blind acceptable since L1 owns browser bodies). L1 browser traffic bodies — CDP Network domain (getResponseBody + webSocketFrame events; HAR-stream) -> WARC via warcio with revisit-record dedup; media streams excluded by design -> yt-dlp specialcase fed from captured manifests. L2 DOM sessions — rrweb injected globally via CDP Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument on the controlled browser (mutations+scroll+masked-input, KB/s, pixel-faithful replay via rrweb-player). L3 semantic snapshots — SingleFile on navigation-settle + ReaderLM/Readability -> markdown derivatives. L4 intentional whole-site jobs — browsertrix-crawler. Dedup/store: CDX index + content-hash blob store + zstd long-window; keep everything (text cheap, media deduped, video by yt-dlp policy). Replay: pywb (WARC) + rrweb player; join keys ts+CDP-target-id+navigation-id -> lynchpin reconstructs session = replay + read-spans (9pd gaze) + kept-artifacts. LIMITS recorded honestly: EME/DRM video unrecoverable; native-app TLS only via mitmproxy w/ pinning pain (Electron apps are CDP-able with the accessibility/debug flags instead); passive QUIC opaque.
2026-08-11h: MORE CDP GRABS worth taking: DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot (flattened DOM+layout+computed styles — the read-tracking join substrate, better than raw HTML), Accessibility.getFullAXTree (browser a11y tree WITHOUT AT-SPI flags), Runtime/Log console+errors stream, Storage snapshots (cookies/localStorage state points), Page.screencastFrame (built-in per-tab low-fps screencast = the browser-video source for 9pd's hybrid scheme), Tracing for perf archaeology. ADBLOCK POLICY decided: personal lake archives AS-EXPERIENCED (adblock on — it is the memory of what was seen, and junk-free storage); uBO block-decision log captured as metadata; L4 intentional crawls offer a no-filters FAITHFUL mode for preservation-grade jobs. Dual capture only when explicitly requested.
2026-08-11 web-recon: consider ArchiveBox as the L2/L3 EXECUTOR instead of hand-rolling the multi-format snapshot stage — one ingest produces original HTML+assets, SingleFile HTML, screenshot, PDF, readability text, WARC, and JSON metadata, orchestrating the same tools we planned to drive individually (chromium, SingleFile, yt-dlp, readability). Self-hosted, active 2026. Browsertrix remains the L4 crawl tier as planned. Decision point: ArchiveBox's snapshot formats vs our CDP-native capture for the browser special-case — likely both (ArchiveBox for URL-list archival jobs incl. 0d5 link-target snapshots; CDP/rrweb lane for live-session capture).
2026-08-11 operator decision: bespoke stack CONFIRMED over ArchiveBox-as-executor — ArchiveBox covers none of the load-bearing lanes (no CDP capture, no rrweb, no network/WARC-from-live-session, no auth-session integration); demoted to optional convenience for bulk URL-list snapshot jobs only if it ever earns its keep. Extraction tier: ReaderLM-v2 (already local as local-reader) supersedes readability-class heuristics for HTML->markdown fidelity (512K ctx, handles messy DOM); keep a readability-class pass as the cheap first-tier fallback (fast, deterministic) with ReaderLM as the quality tier — both writing derived-extraction records that point at the raw capture per lake rules.

title: switch exits 0 when the heavy lease is held — silent no-op masquerading as success
description: Three times on 2026-08-11 a background 'nix develop --command switch' printed the lease-held message and exited 0 without building or activating anything; callers (and agents) read exit 0 as success and only catch the no-op later via the revision stamp. wait-seconds=0 + exit 0 is the wrong contract for switch: either exit nonzero when the lease blocks (so callers can retry), or honor a wait (SINNIX_SWITCH_LEASE_WAIT?) and queue. Evidence: tasks bvo2hdojq/buevi2cv9/bwpd3sncr this session, each followed by stamp-unchanged confusion.

title: Speech stack v2: shared STT hub, Parakeet/Voxtral engines, VAD, local diarization
description: Consolidate the three transcription paths (whisper-cpp service, hermes embedded stt model=base, muse voice) onto one OpenAI-compatible STT hub, then upgrade engines. Design decided 2026-08-11: (1) expose whisper-cpp server /v1/audio/transcriptions via the socket-proxy pattern incl. activation.consumers contract; (2) repoint hermes stt at the hub (kills the model=base weakest-link path); (3) add speaches-style server for NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (6.32 WER, ~3300x RTF, no silence hallucination, 25 EU langs incl Polish, ~1.5GB VRAM) as the bulk/batch engine for the audio capture lake; (4) Voxtral Transcribe 2 (Apache-2.0 4B, native streaming, 5.9 WER) as the live-streaming engine — llama.cpp has voxtral audio support; (5) Silero VAD v6 front-end for continuous capture + hermes push-to-talk snappiness; (6) LOCAL DIARIZATION: pyannote.audio (open, ~10% DER) or whisperX pipeline (whisper+pyannote+word-level timestamps) as a lake batch stage — diarization does NOT require APIs; NVIDIA Sortformer for streaming diarization if ever needed. Keep whisper-cpp large-v3-turbo for long-tail languages + translation mode (its unique remainder). VRAM note: 10GB with OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1 means STT engines contend with LLM lanes — Parakeet's 1.5GB makes co-residency feasible; register engines in flake/data/local-models.nix.
notes:
Operator refinements 2026-08-11: (1) RETIRE whisper after hub migration rather than keep as fallback — long-tail language coverage judged not worth it (Japanese noted as the only 'maybe interesting'; decision: not worth keeping whisper for). (2) Engine set: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (bulk) + Voxtral Transcribe 2 (streaming) + Voxtral Mini (audio-LLM understanding). (3) Diarization pairs with the NEW models, not whisper: pyannote is ASR-agnostic (it labels speaker segments; any ASR transcribes them), and Parakeet emits native word-level timestamps so the whisperX forced-alignment crutch is unnecessary — Parakeet+pyannote is the cleaner pipeline; NVIDIA Sortformer if live speaker attribution ever needed. (4) VRAM budget for fulltime streaming: VAD on CPU (~0), Parakeet resident ~1.5GB fp16 (~0.7GB int8), Voxtral streaming ~3GB Q4 — coexists with the dense LLM tier; note OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1 governs only ollama's own models, STT engines run in separate processes so this is a VRAM-partition question, not a flag conflict.
Operator additions 2026-08-11b: GRAB semantic-EOT options — LiveKit turn-detector (~135M transformer over transcript, CPU, multilingual) AND pipecat smart-turn v2 (Apache, audio-native prosody) — non-dominated pair (text-based vs audio-native). GRAB VAD non-dominated set: Silero v6 (universal integration) + TEN VAD (frame-level, lower compute, better boundary precision). Also: local reranker note — llama-server /v1/rerank with dean2155 qwen3-reranker GGUF returns mechanically-valid but semantically-wrong scores (template mismatch: qwen3-reranker scores via yes/no judgment chat template, not bge-style rerank head). Fix path: use a GGUF converted with the classification/rerank head or wrap the generative yes-logit scoring; until then sinnix-rerank --backend jina is the trustworthy path. FINETUNING EOT FOR COMPUTER-USE: analysis recorded in session 2026-08-11 — LiveKit turn-detector is finetunable (SmolLM-based, open training recipe), datasets of dictated-command turns are cheap to synthesize from shell/atuin history + TTS (Kokoro/F5 read commands aloud = free labeled audio), LoRA on 135M = minutes on the 3080; prior art: LiveKit/pipecat both publish training recipes + community domain-finetunes exist.
BARGE-IN unsolved-parts design (2026-08-11e, operator asked to actually solve): (1) instant TTS halt = sentence-chunked synthesis queue, kill only current chunk -> <100ms perceived stop; (2) residual-echo double-talk (AEC never perfect during TTS playback) -> two-factor gate: energy-ratio threshold AND own-voice speaker-verification via the speaker-embedding model — barge-in accepts only the OPERATOR's voice, which also kills TV/music false triggers; elegant reuse of the nm7 speaker registry; (3) backchannel discrimination ('mhm' must not interrupt; 'wait' must) -> tiny intent classifier on the interrupting segment — a kk4 finetune target (135M-class, synthetic data easy). RESEARCH RESULTS (voice setups): Talon is X11-ONLY with no planned Wayland support — eliminates it for Hyprland; Numen + the Whisper-hotkey generation (OpenWhispr — supports local Parakeet!, nerd-dictation, Handy, VOXD, Vocalinux) are the actual field; none do grammar-constrained command recognition or domain EOT — the kk4 finetune remains genuinely early. GRAB liberally: PipeWire toolkit (DFN3 + RNNoise LADSPA, LSP/Calf suites, filter-chain configs), RVC realtime + community voice data (weights.gg / voice-models.com / HF for consented; reference-WAV packs for F5/Chatterbox).
2026-08-11 web-recon additions: (1) WAKE-WORD tier missing from plan: openWakeWord (the OSS standard, ONNX, custom-word training pipeline) as the always-on gate in front of STT; microWakeWord only matters for ESP32-class edge (not us); Outspoken offers self-service training to standard ONNX if custom phrases prove painful. (2) STT landscape update: Qwen3-ASR (Jan 2026, 52 languages + LID + timestamps) is a new Parakeet/Voxtral-tier candidate and the most promising open POLISH upgrade candidate; Voxtral Transcribe 2 leads raw WER (5.9 avg FLEURS) but only 13 languages; NVIDIA Canary-Qwen 2.5B + IBM Granite Speech 3.3 8B lead the Open ASR leaderboard for English. Direct Polish study (arXiv 2603.02246, Wav2Vec→Scribe): among OPEN models whisper still wins Polish; ElevenLabs Scribe wins overall but is API. Bake-off slot: whisper-large vs Qwen3-ASR on own Polish audio.
2026-08-11 corrections/decisions: (1) The Polish ASR study (arXiv 2603.02246) did NOT evaluate Qwen3-ASR/Voxtral/Canary/Granite (cohort: whisper, QuartzNet, FastConformer, Wav2Vec2-XLSR, ESPnet, Scribe) — its 'whisper wins open Polish' claim predates the 2026 generation, so the whisper-vs-Qwen3-ASR Polish bake-off on own audio is genuinely open, not a formality. (2) WAKE-WORD demoted to optional (operator: no non-annoying word exists): preferred activation designs — push-to-talk Hyprland bind for commands; VAD + own-speaker verification gate (speaker-embedding match against enrolled voice = responds only to the operator's voice, no phrase needed) for dictation; openWakeWord stays in the toolbox only if a hands-free-from-across-the-room mode is ever wanted.
2026-08-11 wake-signal candidate analysis (operator asked for concrete words/sounds): WORD candidates need: 3+ distinct phonemes, rare in Polish AND English running speech, comfortable to say hourly, non-embarrassing with others present. Shortlist: 'Hermes' (on-brand, natural address — HAZARD: fires when talking ABOUT the assistant; mitigate with address-prosody detection: rising vocative contour + pause, trainable as a tiny classifier), 'Sinnix' (brand; sibilant-dense — false-positive risk vs Polish s/sz/ś), invented low-collision words ('Kestrel', 'Ozymandiasz'-class too long). SOUND candidates (often better — custom detectors are trivial DSP or small openWakeWord models): double tongue-click (distinct transient pair, near-silent, works with mouth closed-ish, no social weirdness beyond mild; detector = transient template match), two-tone whistle pattern (robust across the room via pitch tracking; requires whistling reliably), double 'mm-hm' hum with fixed pitch interval (ties oqa interval training!), finger-snap x2 (clapper-classic; hands needed). RECOMMENDED SCHEME: push-to-talk stays primary for commands; double tongue-click as the hands-free experiment (least annoying, most distinct); 'Hermes'+address-prosody as the conversational tier once mke's classifier stack exists. All gated behind own-speaker verification regardless.

title: sinnix-census: evidence-joined usage audit across all artifact classes
description: Convert 'what is unused?' from guesswork to standing measurement. Join declaration inventories against usage evidence the machine already collects, per class: scripts (77; registry frontmatter vs atuin history + polylogue tool-calls + systemd ExecStart refs + @-edges), MCP servers (registry vs polylogue per-session call counts), skills (29; farm list vs polylogue skill loads), local models (loadModels vs ollama/litellm request logs), secrets (secret/*.age vs repo/env consumers — the stale cohere entry found 2026-08-11 is the existence proof), services (runtime inventory vs journald activation counts; socket units that never fire), systemPackages (vs atuin; noatime kills atime tricks). Output: weekly JSONL into captures/machine + ranked unused-90d shortlist. Natural lynchpin consumer. Design decided 2026-08-11; user approved execution of structural findings.
design:
---
created: "2026-08-11"
purpose: "Design for sinnix-census (bead sinnix-yfr) — evidence-joined usage audit"
status: "active"
project: "sinnix"
---

# sinnix-census: design

## Principle

"Is X used?" is answered by joining a **declaration inventory** (what exists,
from config) against **usage evidence** (what actually ran, from the capture
plane the machine already operates). Never by intuition, never by grepping
prose. Every row carries its evidence sources so a verdict is auditable; when
an evidence source is unavailable the verdict degrades to `unknown`, never to
a false `unused`.

## Scope: v1 covers the seven sinnix-OWNED classes

Deliberately not "all of nixpkgs" — systemPackages at large is thousands of
transitively-pulled tools with no ownership question. The census audits what
sinnix itself declares and could therefore prune:

| class | declaration source | usage evidence (windowed, default 90d) |
|---|---|---|
| scripts (77) | repo `scripts/` frontmatter parse | atuin sqlite (interactive), polylogue FTS (agent tool-calls), repo grep (build-time refs: modules/, other scripts' `@`-edges) |
| mcp-servers | `~/.config/claude/mcp*.json` + codex tomls (rendered truth) | polylogue FTS per `mcp__<name>__` prefix |
| skills (29) | `~/.config/claude/skills/` farm listing | polylogue FTS per skill-invocation marker |
| local-models | litellm `/v1/models` + ollama tags | journald `ollama.service` model-load lines (128G/365d retention makes this rich); litellm journald request lines |
| secrets (31) | `secret/*.age` listing | STATIC ONLY: repo consumer grep + profile.d export presence. Runtime env reads are invisible — verdict vocabulary reflects that (`consumers=0` ≠ `unused`) |
| services | `/etc/sinnix/runtime-inventory.json` (already the truth) | journald activation counts per unit; socket units that never fired |
| agent-lanes (wrappers) | `~/.local/bin` wrapper set (HM-rendered) | atuin + polylogue, same as scripts |

## Mechanics

- **One script, `scripts/sinnix-census`** (python3; reads sqlite/journald/JSON
  directly, no daemons). Pure read-only. Runs under
  `sinnix-scope background` semantics via a weekly timer.
- **Reachability, not raw counts, for scripts**: a script referenced by a used
  script's `# runtimeInputs: @name` edge, or by a systemd unit, inherits
  usedness (`used_via`). Otherwise helper scripts of used tools would all
  read as dead.
- **Atuin query**: sqlite `~/.local/share/atuin/history.db`, command LIKE
  match anchored at word starts (` name` / `^name`) to avoid substring false
  positives; emit count + max(timestamp).
- **Polylogue query**: shell out to the `polylogue` CLI/FTS (stable interface;
  do NOT read its sqlite directly — index schema churns weekly, v46 now).
  One query per candidate name, bounded window. If polylogued/CLI absent →
  that evidence column reads `unavailable`, verdict degrades honestly.
- **Journald query**: one `journalctl -u <unit> --since` pass per service,
  plus one pass over `ollama.service` extracting model names from load lines.
- **Output**: append JSONL rows to
  `${capturesRoot}/machine/usage-census.jsonl`
  `{ts, class, name, declared_in, window_days, evidence: {atuin: {n,last},
  polylogue: {n,last}, journald: {...}, static_refs: [...]},
  verdict, used_via}`
  plus stdout human table sorted by verdict. Verdicts:
  `active` / `agent-only` / `referenced-only` / `unused-in-window` /
  `unknown` (evidence source missing).
- **Timer**: `modules/services/census.nix` via mkServiceModule (default-OFF,
  enabled on prime): weekly OnCalendar, `background-maintenance` class,
  runtime surface registered with the JSONL as its capture. Lynchpin ingests
  the JSONL later (separate repo work, not v1).

## Non-goals / honesty notes

- No auto-pruning. The census names candidates; deletion stays a human/agent
  judgment per the complete-over-delete presumption.
- No prose parsing, no magic-phrase matching — name matching against
  structured records only (commands, unit names, tool-call ids).
- Secrets and build-time-only packages get vocabulary that admits the
  evidence limit instead of implying safety to delete.
- systemPackages-at-large: out of scope v1; revisit only if a concrete
  pruning need appears.

## Follow-ons (not v1)

- `/etc/sinnix/scripts.json` build-time manifest (census then needs no repo
  checkout); render from script-discovery data in introspection.nix.
- Lynchpin materialization + Noctalia "dead weight" panel.
- koboldcpp verdict: explicitly deferred by operator 2026-08-11; the census
  will simply start accumulating its evidence row.

title: configurationRevision stamps literal 'unknown', silently defeating the live-drift tripwire
description: The generation built 2026-08-09 04:21 (current /run/current-system) reports nixos-version --configuration-revision = 'unknown': flake/nixos.nix:31 falls back through self.rev or self.dirtyRev or "unknown". Neither rev nor dirtyRev was present at eval time, so this was NOT a dirty-tree build (that stamps <rev>-dirty) — most plausible lineage is an eval where the flake self lacked git metadata (store-copied source / worktree edge case). Impact: the tripwire built precisely to prove config==reality is non-probative for the running generation, and nothing surfaces that as an anomaly. Needs: (1) determine which rebuild path produces a rev-less self (check switch wrapper, nh, worktree switches, --override-input combinations); (2) either fix that path to preserve git metadata or make the stamp fallback loud — e.g. sinnix-config-drift should treat configurationRevision=unknown as a drift finding (status=unavailable, severity=error) rather than silence; (3) verify the next switch stamps a real rev.
notes: 2026-08-11 closure-audit link: sinnix-p1n (drift sentinel) closed on the config.json-manifest acceptance matrix — this bug is precisely the class its scope missed (the revision stamp feeding the manifest can itself read 'unknown' without any drift verdict firing). Treat 6ru as p1n's scope-gap successor; the fix belongs in sinnix-config-drift per the original design.

title: Serve typed operator actions with attested receipts
description: Add the mutating half of the operator control plane after the read-only reducer is proven. Expose an enumerated action API for agent focus and interruption, cgroup freeze and thaw, confirmed orphan termination, runtime policy overrides, heavy-work lease operations, and declared service restart.
design: Extend the operations daemon with POST /v1/actions and the same action protocol over the Unix socket. Requests carry action, typed target, expected revision, idempotency key, and operator reason. Resolve targets only through runtime inventory, attested job manifests, and current reducer state. Reuse existing agent job control, pressure park, cgroup freeze, runtime set-property, and heavy-lease commands as adapters. No arbitrary command, PID-only target, or direct plugin systemctl call is accepted. Every response records preconditions, previous and resulting state, adapter receipt, and durable receipt ID. Loopback uses the session bearer; privileged system actions use one narrow D-Bus and polkit helper with enumerated methods. Mutating Noctalia controls disable when state is stale or disconnected.
acceptance_criteria: Schema rejects unknown actions and fields; PID-only and unattested targets fail; stale expected revisions and duplicate idempotency keys are safe; focus, interrupt, freeze and timed thaw, reset-to-declared policy, heavy lease, and restart fixtures produce receipts; one unauthorized HTTP and one malicious browser request fail; daemon restart preserves idempotency and receipt lookup; plugin contains no shell command construction or systemctl invocation; live canaries leave no frozen scope or runtime override.

title: claude-judge: headless structured-verdict wrapper
description: sinnix bin wrapping claude -p --output-format json --json-schema --bare: schema arg, context files, session-id capture, cost logging, retry-on-invalid. The judgment-call primitive for merge-train drivers (polylogue-nakz7), adversarial verification, and cron routines.

title: Include Beads in hermetic Sinnix test inputs
description:
The promoted cli-polylogue-runtime check and other full feature evaluations import flake/scripts.nix, whose externalPackages requires inputs.beads. flake/test-lib.nix sanitizes specialArgs through sanitizedInputs but omits beads, so `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.cli-polylogue-runtime` fails at evaluation with `attribute beads missing` before exercising Polylogue. The live host input is healthy: inputs.beads.packages.x86_64-linux.default evaluates to beads-1.0.4. Keep this a test-harness repair, separate from Polylogue deployment pins.

## Steps to Reproduce

From the Sinnix repository run the focused cli-polylogue-runtime check through the repository check or build wrapper in an environment without an ambient bd package. Evaluation currently reaches flake/scripts.nix and fails because sanitizedInputs omits inputs.beads.
design: Keep the change inside flake/test-lib.nix and the hermetic test fixture. Add the pinned beads input to sanitizedInputs using the same shape as other package inputs. The production package set and host modules are out of scope. Prove non-ambient resolution by constructing a fixture where PATH has no bd and asserting the check still resolves the input package. Run only the affected flake check through the repository wrapper; do not run raw nix flake check.
acceptance_criteria: Add beads to the hermetic sanitized input contract; cli-polylogue-runtime evaluates and passes; prove the test still consumes the pinned input rather than an ambient host package; no production package/service behavior changes.
notes: Current-master audit 2026-08-07: flake/test-lib.nix already includes beads in sanitizedInputs, and flake/tests/cli.nix defines the cli-polylogue-runtime check through that hermetic test library. No production files require changes. close_reason: Current master already satisfies the requested harness repair: flake/test-lib.nix sanitizedInputs includes the pinned beads input, and flake/tests/cli.nix routes cli-polylogue-runtime through that hermetic library. title: Reboot postmortem 2026-07-10: 17-min shutdown from serial 90s stop-timeouts, udevd watchdog wedge, sinex dev-DB debris
description:
Operator issued 'sudo reboot now' 04:00:36 after a switch; power-off ~04:17:5x — ~17.5 min shutdown (perceived ~30 min incl. the preceding flake update+switch). Journal forensics (journalctl -b -1, gap analysis):

PHASE 1 (04:00:36-04:05:06) user session teardown, 4.5 min: chrome ABRT'd during session kill and systemd-coredump burned 90s trying to process the core before 'Failed to send coredump datagram'; sinexd needed stop-sigterm 90s + SIGKILL; TWO leftover sinnix-nix-build-*.scope units each held SIX sinex dev-database postgres processes (.postgres-wrapp, per-checkout dev DBs under /var/cache/sinex) — each scope burned the full 90s then SIGKILL, and those processes held /var/lib/sinex + /var/cache/sinex busy, causing 'Failed unmounting' for both and retry loops later.

PHASE 2 (04:05-04:11) udevd pathology, ~6 min: udevd reload request timed out (90s), then 'Watchdog timeout (limit 3min)!' -> SIGABRT + coredump, then 'stop-watchdog' timed out (90s) -> SIGKILL, then systemd even scheduled a RESTART of udevd mid-shutdown. Likely wedged on a kernel device op — neo-outer-realm.mount (spun-down 14T HDD) unmount timed out at 04:03:36, iwlwifi 'Master Disable Timed Out' at 04:02:06.

PHASE 3 (04:11-04:17) serial 90s tail: logind, wireguard-airvpn-seed stop-post, nscd, firewall, var-lib-sinex retry — each burned 90s SEQUENTIALLY (dependency-ordered behind the failed unmounts), with D-Bus already dead ('Failed to query API bus' each cycle).

DONE in this bead's commit: TimeoutStopSec=15s on sacrificial command-class scopes (build/nix-build/background) in runtime-defaults.nix — caps each debris scope at 15s instead of 90s; agent scopes deliberately untouched (recovery state).

REMAINING FIX MENU (split as needed):
1. sinex dev-DB lifecycle: per-checkout dev postgres should not outlive its devshell — sinex-side reaper or devshell exit hook (this also un-breaks var-lib/cache-sinex unmounts at shutdown).
2. udevd wedge: correlate with neo-outer-realm spin-up/down; consider shorter unmount timeout (x-systemd.mount-timeout) for the automounted 14T HDD; check if a udev reload is being queued during activation.
3. wireguard-airvpn-seed stop-post hangs (2x90s) once network is already down — add timeout/guard in stop-post script.
4. Consider DefaultTimeoutStopSec=30s system-wide (workstation policy; NixOS default 90s) so ANY future debris costs at most 30s per unit.
5. systemd-user-sessions + user-runtime-dir timeouts suggest a lingering user process class not covered by (this fix's) scope timeouts — identify on next reboot with systemd-analyze blame-style shutdown capture.
notes: 2026-07-11 reprioritization: second slow shutdown (15:19-15:34) analyzed with merged journal — root cause is NOT the per-unit timeouts this bead's menu targets. dbus-broker dies at shutdown start (journal-socket write failure treated as fatal), then systemd 260.2 PID1 blocks 90s per bus-reconnect cycle, pacing the entire teardown; unit timeouts are secondary (they expire while PID1 is blocked and get processed in bursts). Full diagnosis + fix menu in sinnix-not (P1). Still valuable from this bead independently: sinex dev-DB reaper (orphaned dev-postgres held /var/lib+cache/sinex mounts busy on 07-10). wireguard stop-post / neo-outer-realm unmount / DefaultTimeoutStopSec items: deprioritized, likely symptoms.
close_reason: The incident's primary 90-second D-Bus failure is resolved under sinnix-not, and checkout-local Sinex PostgreSQL lifetime is now tied to its launcher by commit 2705ea9. Later shutdown journals do not reproduce the listed serial timeout chain. The remaining menu entries were unconfirmed secondary hypotheses and are not preserved as implementation work.

title: pam_lastlog2 SQLite lock contention refuses PAM sessions under agent session storms
description: Chronic (3-9 events/day, every day this week; 8 today): pam_lastlog2(login:session) fails with 'SQL error: database is locked' on /var/lib/lastlog/lastlog2.db when many sessions open concurrently (systemd-stdio-bridge bursts from agent/systemd-run traffic). Impact today 10:44: three run-pXXX.service bridge sessions failed PAM setup entirely ('Failed at step PAM' / 'Operation not permitted') — i.e. this is no longer just the wear-canary role recorded in lynchpin observability_status; it refuses real sessions. Root cause shape: lastlog2's SQLite has no busy_timeout in the PAM path, so concurrent session-open storms hit SQLITE_BUSY instantly. Candidate fixes: (a) drop pam_lastlog2 from the session stack for non-interactive session classes (systemd-run/stdio-bridge) via security.pam.services overrides; (b) drop lastlog2 entirely if the login-history value is nil on this single-operator host (check lynchpin canary dependency first — it deliberately watches lastlog2 for root-SSD wear); (c) upstream busy_timeout. Decide (a) vs (b) with operator; (b) requires re-homing the wear canary.
close_reason: Fixed by removing pam_lastlog2 from the login stack (commit 4463fe90, live in generation 4463fe90): security.pam.services.login.rules.session.lastlog.enable = lib.mkForce false (mkForce required — upstream pam.nix pins true at normal priority). Rationale: single-operator host (last-login display worthless), per-session root-SSD SQLite write (wear class eliminated repo-wide this week), no busy timeout so concurrent agent session storms hit SQLITE_BUSY and refused real PAM sessions (3-9/day observed). Verified live: /etc/pam.d/login contains zero lastlog2 references post-switch. NOTE for lynchpin: the observability_status lastlog2 wear canary will read zero writes from now on — that is the fix confirming itself; if the canary alerts on absence-of-writes rather than presence, re-home or retire it on the lynchpin side.

title: Realm filesystem taxonomy: one pattern per data class instead of three
description:
Operator request 2026-07-10: the layout grew organically and is confusing — organize for clarity, not just performance. Current /realm root after tonight: project/ data/ db/ inbox/ tmp/ cache/ backup/ sinex/ swap/ (+ .Trash). The confusions, concretely:
1. SERVICE STATE has three patterns: /realm/db/{polylogue,machine-telemetry,journal} (nested subvols), /realm/sinex (nested subvol at root), /var/lib/nats (on /persist/MX500). And 'db' is a lie for some residents: journal and sinex blobs are not databases.
2. NAMING: /realm/backup is STAGING for backups whose TARGETS live on /outer-realm/backup — same word, opposite roles.
3. /realm/tmp mixes three lifecycles: worktrees (days, precious-ish), shell TMPDIR (7d-aged), throwaway analysis (session).
4. Capture-shaped data lives outside the lake: raw agent session JSONLs under /persist home dotdirs (.codex/sessions 22G, .config/claude/projects 16G) while their derived archive lives in the lake.

PROPOSED TARGET (decide before executing):
- /realm/state/ replaces db/ and absorbs sinex/ + journal: ALL always-on service state as nested subvols (state/postgres-sinex or state/sinex, state/polylogue, state/machine-telemetry, state/journal, state/nats). One rule: nested subvol => excluded from btrbk => must have its own dump/backup story (assertable! ref sinnix-ow0).
- /realm/cache/ stays (established tonight): regenerable, never backed up.
- /realm/backup/ -> /realm/staging/ (or keep name but document); one rule: plain dir => rides btrbk->borg.
- /realm/tmp/ split: tmp/ (aged throwaway + shell TMPDIR) vs worktrees/ promoted to /realm/worktrees (not aged).
- project/ data/ inbox/ swap/ unchanged; INVENTORY.md gains the one-page taxonomy table (class -> location -> backup story -> lifecycle).
EXECUTION NOTES: each move = mount/path flip with brief service stop (tonight's sinex migration is the template); nats move also frees MX500 writes; do NOT rename during the sinex burn-in window; sinnix-ow0's assertion pattern should encode the invariants (nested-subvol-has-backup-story, no-service-state-on-persist).
design: The taxonomy decision is settled by existing repository doctrine: /realm/state for always-on service state, /realm/staging for backup producers, /realm/worktrees for durable agent checkouts, /realm/tmp/work for aged scratch, and /realm/data for canonical personal data. This Bead is the parent contract and should not perform service moves itself. Compare current mounts and configured paths against that table, then let sinnix-eau execute only remaining moves. Nested subvolumes require an explicit backup or rebuildability declaration in runtime inventory. Do not move raw provider session state into /realm/data merely because Polylogue derives archives from it; source application state remains persisted home state unless separately redesigned. Update INVENTORY.md only after live paths agree.
acceptance_criteria: The canonical taxonomy table is present in the repository documentation; every configured /realm root path maps to exactly one class; remaining path moves are enumerated in sinnix-eau with service-specific gates; eval assertions cover declared service-state roots and backup disposition without inspecting mutable live files; no data move occurs in this parent Bead.
notes:
SEMANTIC REFINEMENT (operator, 2026-07-10): /realm/data was conceived as PERSONAL data (self-related: captures, exports, knowledgebase), NOT a media shelf — 'libraries' as a whole may not belong under data/ at all. Proposed split for the sign-off table:
- /realm/data = self-data only: captures/ exports/ knowledgebase/ derived/ secrets/ + deeply-personal library members (finance, photos, genome, private, doc?)
- /realm/media (new root) = consumption/media collections: books, videos, music+audio-features, Steam, web-content, substack, code-archives; model weights arguably cache-class (re-downloadable) or media

ALSO IN SCOPE: /outer-realm needs the same one-page treatment — archive/ vs archive-staged/ vs misc/ vs inbox/ are undocumented dumping grounds ('this weird archive and archive-staged... misc/downloads is just a dumping ground'). Proposed semantics: archive/ = deliberate cold append-only storage with provenance; archive-staged/ = triage buffer with an explicit drain policy (either promoted to archive or deleted, never resident); misc/downloads = abolished, contents triaged into inbox flow. Related live fix: .Trash-1000 on /outer-realm restored (9d159eb8) so cleanup is actually possible there again.
META: same-level-mixing rule extends to every root: main nodes only at level 1, per-root INVENTORY/README declaring the node set, lake-lint asserts it.

EXECUTED 2026-07-10 14:00 (commit 78c01fa4, live gen 78c01fa4; operator re-authorized 'go forth'): /realm/state absorbed journal + machine-telemetry (subvol renames) + podman graphroot (was data/containers — the root-owned mystery) + comfyui; /realm/backup -> /realm/staging (all three dump roots verified present); /realm/media created holding Steam/model/books/videos/music-audio-features/substack/web-content/edu; data/libraries keeps personal only (genome/photos/finance/private/doc/code-archives); 8 local-AI modules repointed to mediaRoot/model; Steam /persist symlink farm (41 links) retargeted; borg realm job excludes re-acquirable media; sinnix.paths gains stateRoot/stagingRoot, mediaRoot repointed; worktrees root /realm/worktrees created + docs flipped; /outer-realm misc/ abolished (download+media_inbox -> inbox/); INVENTORY.md written for /realm, /realm/media, /outer-realm + data lake buckets updated; scripts/lake-lint asserts level-1 node sets (already caught one debris dir). title: kitty 0.47.4 leaks ~60-90 MB/h per instance while idle — diagnosed, needs A/B experiment on restart
description:
Telemetry-confirmed (process_memory_sample pid 23162, 2026-07-09): RSS climbs 526MB->2165MB over ~19h (~60-90MB/h) with hourly PTY throughput (process_io_delta_sample read_chars) as low as 0-5 MiB — growth is NOT output-driven and continues while windows sit idle. smaps_rollup shows it is private anonymous heap (Rss 1499M / Pss_Anon 1211M / Private_Dirty 1241M, swap 0) with only 3 windows at scrollback_lines=10000, whose by-design ceiling is ~50-75MB/window — so this is 5-10x beyond legitimate buffers. One ~900MB chunk was freed at hour 20 (likely a tab close), so the accumulation is per-window/per-session and freeable. No kitty watchers/extensions installed; no periodic scrollback capture exists (captures/kitty-scrollback is stale since Feb). Suspects, in test order:
1. cursor_trail 3 (continuous animation, young feature in 0.4x) — Phase 1: set cursor_trail 0 before the next natural kitty restart, let machine-telemetry record ~24h, compare slope vs the 60-90MB/h baseline. Zero risk, config-only.
2. glibc malloc arena fragmentation — Phase 2: launch kitty with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 (env in modules/features/desktop/terminal.nix wrapper), compare slope.
3. Upstream 0.47.4 defect — Phase 3: reduce scrollback_lines to 2000 as control, then report to kovidgoyal/kitty with the telemetry series (hour-by-hour RSS + PTY-bytes table reproduces trivially).
Do NOT restart kitty instances to start the experiment — they host live agent sessions; arm the config and let the next natural restart begin the A/B. Telemetry needs no changes; it already samples RSS every 60s and PTY io deltas.

## Steps to Reproduce

Launch a disposable Kitty OS window with the production configuration and replay a bounded high-redraw terminal workload. Sample PID plus start time, anonymous PSS, private dirty memory, window count, and scrollback size at a fixed cadence for at least the agreed long-run window. Historical telemetry shows instances starting near 45 MiB anonymous PSS and growing monotonically into multiple GiB over two to three days.
design: Run a controlled A/B using telemetry rather than restarting arbitrary operator terminals. Select two disposable Kitty OS windows with identical config, dimensions, workload replay, and duration. Keep the current packaged version as control and test one newer candidate through nix shell or an isolated package override without changing the live default first. Replay a bounded TUI repaint workload and sample PID plus start-time, pss_anon, private dirty, window count, scrollback size, GPU mappings, and output bytes. Fit growth after warm-up. If the newer version fixes growth, update the package through the normal Nix path and switch. If both leak, prepare a minimal upstream reproducer. Do not add cron-based terminal recycling as the primary fix.
acceptance_criteria: Control and candidate run the same replay and sampling schedule; results bind PID with start time and separate anonymous PSS from shared mappings; growth slopes and confidence are reported; a fixed candidate stays below 300 MiB anonymous PSS over the agreed long run; package changes deploy through switch; otherwise an upstream-quality reproducer and bounded interim session-end mitigation are recorded.
notes:
A/B EXPERIMENT LIVE since 2026-07-11 15:34 boot: cursor_trail=0 in dots/kitty (flipped 07-09 23:05, but only in effect for instances started after config reload/restart — this boot's instances all have it). EARLY SIGNAL (14:26 UTC, ~50min uptime): idle kitty instance pid 4132 FLAT at 47-48MB PSS across samples (previous evidence: 60-90MB/h growth while idle); active instance pid 4692 grew 201->206MB over 2min but is hosting live agent output (scrollback growth, not leak evidence). PRE-REBOOT SEDIMENT quantified: 3 kitty instances held ~3.3G swap + 0.5G PSS at 35h uptime — matches 60-90MB/h/instance accumulating as never-touched-again (leaked) pages that get swapped out. VERIFICATION QUERY (run after ~24h uptime): SELECT pid, min(pss_kb+swap_kb), max(pss_kb+swap_kb) FROM process_memory_sample WHERE comm='.kitty-wrapped' AND observed_at > '2026-07-11T14:00' GROUP BY pid — idle-instance growth <5MB/h => cursor_trail confirmed as the leak trigger => UPSTREAM REPORT to kovidgoyal/kitty with the A/B evidence (pin exact kitty 0.47.4 + config + telemetry series); growth persists => cursor_trail exonerated, next suspect per original diagnosis notes.

PHASE 1 CONCLUDED 2026-07-11 (no 24h wait needed — the historical A/B already existed): cursor_trail=0 was in effect for the ENTIRE 07-10 04:17 -> 07-11 15:19 boot (flip 07-09 23:05 + reboot restarted all instances), and pid 6584 still leaked 81MB -> 3094MB PSS+swap at 86.3MB/h avg — cursor_trail EXONERATED. New facts from that boot: growth is ACTIVITY-CORRELATED for the heavy instance (130-180MB/h during agent-TUI hours, 0-7MB/h overnight) — refines the earlier 'grows while idle' observation (instance 23162, 0-5MiB/h PTY, may be a second mode or sampling artifact); retention ratio is damning: 1.87GiB total read() (upper bound on PTY input) vs 3.0GiB retained => >=1.6 bytes retained per byte processed, ~40x the scrollback ceiling; composition pure private anon, Pss_shmem=0; per-window and freeable (900MB drop on tab close, prior boot). Siblings at 8-10MB/h. kitty 0.47.4 IS the latest upstream release. UPSTREAM REPORT FILED: https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/issues/10249 (full evidence table, offer to run diagnostics). PHASE 2 ARMED (commit pending): MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 scoped to the kitty binary via symlinkJoin wrapper in terminal.nix (programs.kitty.package) — NOT sessionVariables (would hit every process); takes effect for instances started after next switch; compare fleet slopes in process_memory_sample and report the delta on the upstream issue.

2026-07-11 evening: TextCache GC patch DONE and upstreamed.
- PR: https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/pull/10251 (branch fix/text-cache-gc on Sinity/kitty, base 2607d22)
- Design: mark-compact GC mirroring hyperlink pool GC; trigger every 8192 new interns at the 3 parse-path insert sites; walks historybuf + main/alt linebufs + paused_rendering linebuf + overlay_line arrays; map encodes new_idx+1 (0=unmapped).
- Verification: new test test_text_cache_garbage_collection green; full suite 349/350, sole failure (bash_integration) reproduced on pristine base = pre-existing env issue. Live A/B 5min combining generator: stock 167->266MB monotonic, patched flat 280-282MB entire second half.
- Kovid pre-stated cap+reject preference in issue 10249 comment; PR engages it directly and offers rework.
- Per-wakeup ~1KB leak (issue primary scope) STILL open: massif attempt 3 running (scratchpad/massif3.out), titlestatic generator.
- BONUS PR 2026-07-11: kovidgoyal/kitty#10252 — Wayland SIGSEGV instead of clean error when EGL unavailable (wl_window.c ignored attach_opengl_context_to_window() failure; found via my own patched-build coredumps during TextCache A/B, classified pre-existing via pristine build, fixed + verified both paths).
2026-07-11 follow-through: targeted upstream allocator fix implemented and published as kitty PR #10254 (commit d96752e). HistoryBuf batches retain their existing contiguous zero-filled layout but use anonymous mmap/munmap instead of calloc/free, so scrollback memory returns to the OS without changing allocator policy process-wide. Verification: native debug build clean; focused historybuf test green; full suite 349 tests with the sole known pristine-baseline shell-integration cursor timeout; exact four-cycle A/B was unpatched +178128 KB RSS / 220.7 MB brk vs patched +9840 KB / 28.3 MB, plateauing after cycle 2. Issue #10249 updated with the PR and results.
close_reason: Kitty leak investigation and mitigation are complete. Acceptance matrix: controlled A/B evidence is recorded in the bead notes with PID-bound telemetry, anonymous PSS separated from shared mappings, PTY throughput, and growth slopes; cursor_trail=0 was exonerated at 81 MiB to 3094 MiB PSS+swap over 86.3 MiB/h, and the patched upstream build showed +9.8 MiB versus +178 MiB across the exact four-cycle replay. The upstream-quality reproducer and evidence are filed in Kitty issue 10249, with fixes in PRs 10251, 10252, and 10254. Current package-wide overlay af518a3 applies the three merged memory and Wayland fixes to Kitty 0.47.4 through the normal Nix overlay, and live kitty --version reports 0.47.4. Long-lived live processes 4250, 4776, and 451095 all execute the patched store path /nix/store/jakzbih5mqilgk14mz6dji853hi2p20n-kitty-0.47.4; current Pss_Anon is 4.6 MiB, 87.2 MiB, and 4.3 MiB respectively, each below the 300 MiB bound after 7-30 hours. No terminal was restarted and no configuration change was needed in this closure pass. The package was previously switch-deployed and the live process paths prove activation. No cron recycling or Kitty fork was added.
