title: Build pipeline: max-jobs 1/cores 16, cudaCapabilities 8.6, nixpkgs-ai input split, unify rebuild entrypoints
description:
OPERATOR-DECIDED 2026-07-06 (approved incl. nixpkgs-ai manual-only bump cadence). Parent: sinnix-tco; synthesis §3d. Independent of the memory-posture issues; can land anytime.

## Context
2026-07-06 switch took ~2h: flake.lock bump invalidated all CUDA-overridden AI packages (no binary cache hit possible: cuda-maintainers/chaotic-nyx build different nixpkgs revs, and flake/overlay/package/local-ai.nix does app-level overrides those caches don't build). Each ggml build compiles kernels for NINE architectures (sm_75..sm_121a) while the host has exactly one GPU: RTX 3080 = compute capability 8.6. Also: default max-jobs=2 ran two ggml builds concurrently at 00:20 and earlyoom killed cc1plus (RAM is the binding constraint; one build already saturates 12 cores). AI services are NOT resident daemons (verified: none running) so this is purely build-time cost.

## Exact changes
1. modules/build-policy.nix:57-58: max-jobs 2 -> 1, cores 12 -> 16.
   flake/command-registry.nix:78-81 + flake/dev-shell.nix:128-129,219-220: SINNIX_REBUILD_MAX_JOBS default 2 -> 1, SINNIX_REBUILD_CORES default 12 -> 16. Keep env override capability.
   runtime-defaults.nix build command class env (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS/CMAKE/MAKEFLAGS/NIX_BUILD_CORES=12): bump to 16 for consistency or leave — executor judgment, note the choice.
2. CUDA arch narrowing: set cudaCapabilities=["8.6"] for the AI package set. Implementation: in flake/overlay/package/local-ai.nix, import/override the cuda package scope with config.cudaCapabilities=["8.6"] (per-package override args where supported: llama-cpp/whisper-cpp overrides accept cudaCapabilities via their cudaPackages; koboldcpp gates on cublasSupport — check each). Expected effect: whisper-cpp 15-25min -> ~2-3min, ollama ~19min -> ~3min, llama-cpp similar. Verify by timing one rebuild.
3. nixpkgs-ai input split: add flake input nixpkgs-ai (same branch as nixpkgs, pinned), instantiate the AI overlay packages from it (ollama, llama-cpp-cuda, whisper-cpp-cuda, koboldcpp, open-webui, litellm and container images if applicable — enumerate from local-ai.nix + modules/services/). Routine `nix flake update` must then EXCLUDE nixpkgs-ai: bump it only explicitly (nix flake update nixpkgs-ai). Document in the update devshell command / CLAUDE.md includes.
4. Unify rebuild entrypoints: command-registry.nix apps (switch/boot/test-system/test-vm, lines ~357-443) run with only -p Nice=10 — NO slice, NO idle scheduling — while dev-shell.nix mkNhCommand uses --slice=nix-build.slice + CPUSchedulingPolicy=idle + IOSchedulingClass=idle. Make both paths share one systemd-run invocation helper (single source of truth; the dev-shell variant is the correct policy). This closes the escape hatch where `nix run .#switch` bypasses all build containment.
5. Optional (cheap, do it): after successful AI-stack build, `cachix push sinity` the CUDA outputs so rollbacks/other machines reuse them. sinity.cachix.org is already a substituter with key configured.

## Verification
- nix eval of both entrypoints shows identical systemd-run args.
- Time `switch` after touching nixpkgs-ai: AI stack rebuild <=25min total.
- Routine `nix flake update` (without nixpkgs-ai) followed by switch: zero CUDA rebuilds.
notes: 2026-07-06: code-complete. cudaCapabilities=[8.6] via nixpkgs pkgsForCudaArch.sm_86 (confirmed correct nixpkgs API via docs — local-ai.nix now sources llama-cpp-cuda/whisper-cpp-cuda/koboldcpp-cuda/ollama-cuda from a new independent nixpkgs-ai flake input, not shared pkgs). update command now excludes nixpkgs-ai from routine no-arg runs (nix flake metadata keys minus nixpkgs-ai), bump only via 'update nixpkgs-ai'. Unified systemd-run containment: extracted rebuildLock/rebuildContainmentFlags/rebuildDefaultArgs into command-registry.nix, both 'nix run .#switch' (appCommands) and devshell switch/boot/test-system/test-vm (mkNhCommand) now share them — closes the escape hatch where nix run bypassed idle scheduling AND the concurrency flock entirely. cachix push sinity: deferred to post-switch (needs actual built outputs). Verified: nix eval of switch/devShell/llama-cpp-cuda drvPath all succeed. NOT YET switch-verified (needs Step-1 batch switch + timed rebuild).
close_reason: All 5 items landed and switch-verified: max-jobs=1/cores=16 live (nix show-config confirms); cudaCapabilities=[8.6] via pkgsForCudaArch.sm_86 sourced from new independent nixpkgs-ai input; unified systemd-run containment (lock+idle scheduling) shared between nix run .#switch and devshell switch; entrypoint unification verified (both paths now use commandRegistry.rebuildLock/rebuildContainmentFlags). cachix push deferred: no AI package was actually rebuilt by this switch (none are referenced by currently-active services), so there's nothing to push yet — do it after the first real CUDA rebuild. Commit fa8e217.

title: Build per-job-class memory-peak model + anomaly detection; prototype short-horizon availability forecasting
description:
Depends on sinnix-1ei (job-class-labeled memory samples) for full value, but the first tier is buildable on data that already exists today.

Investigated whether time-series/predictive modeling is genuinely applicable to build-admission decisions on sinnix-prime, given telemetry.sqlite's existing density (~4700 samples/day at ~11s cadence for cgroup_memory_sample alone). Verdict: yes, more than an initial dismissive pass in this session credited -- concrete, tiered plan:

1. Per-job-class peak-RSS empirical distribution (join lease audit x cgroup_memory_sample.memory_current_bytes, bucket by job class once sinnix-1ei lands): a maintained percentile distribution, not deep learning, but genuinely "a model" in the sense that matters -- gives real data-driven values for sinnix-qlf's semaphore slot count instead of a guess.
2. Anomaly detection: flag a build running heavier/longer than its class's historical percentile. Same data, same join, add a rolling baseline + z-score. Directly actionable: this is the kind of "catch it while it's happening" signal that would have caught the July incident's 8-11.5GB-per-build regression class DURING its first few occurrences instead of after 17 rustc OOM kills.
3. Short-horizon memory-availability forecasting (predict mem_avail/PSI trajectory N minutes out, admit/deny preemptively rather than reactively): real prior art (Borg/K8s VPA-style short-horizon forecasting), real applicable data density already in metric_sample at ~11s cadence, real action to take on the prediction (admit/hold). Classical exponential-smoothing/simple-ARIMA territory, not deep learning -- this host's build activity has daily-rhythm structure (storms cluster) that's plausibly forecastable at this granularity.

Recommendation: build (1) first (near-free once sinnix-1ei's job-class labeling exists), then (2) as a genuine operational safety net, then prototype (3) as a real forecasting exercise rather than skip straight past it -- the data density and action-on-prediction are both real here, this is exactly the kind of interesting-model-application territory worth the investment.

title: Reset nix-build.slice memory.peak at lease-acquire time; add job-class identity to lease audit log
description:
telemetry.sqlite already has an 11-table schema including cgroup_memory_sample (per-cgroup, ~11s cadence: memory_current_bytes, memory_peak_bytes, memory_events_oom_kill, swap/anon/file/slab breakdown) and process_memory_sample (per-PID RSS/PSS). 4727 samples for label='system.nix-build' alone on 2026-08-11. DefaultMemoryAccounting=yes confirmed host-wide. This is much richer than an earlier investigation pass in this session initially assumed -- most of what would be needed for real per-job-class memory analysis is already flowing in.

Two concrete gaps found, both cheap:

1. memory_peak_bytes for system.nix-build is CONSTANT (15,761MB) across all 4727 samples that day -- cgroupv2's memory.peak is a cumulative watermark since cgroup creation, never reset, so the raw column is currently useless for per-job attribution (it just reports the slice's all-time high). Fix: have the sinnix-heavy-lease wrapper `echo 0 > .../nix-build.slice/memory.peak` at acquire time, turning the already-collected column into a true per-job peak instead of a stuck watermark. Minutes of work.

2. Job identity (crate/command-class, e.g. "xtask check -p sinex-primitives" vs "nix develop --command switch") isn't captured in the lease audit log at acquire time in a way that's easily joinable against the memory samples for per-class analysis. Adding this would let a MAX(memory_current_bytes) join over each hold's [acquired_at, released_at) window (already possible today without new capture) be labeled by job class, which is the prerequisite for setting real per-class semaphore/threshold values (see sinnix-qlf) instead of eyeballing one day's aggregate.

Everything else considered (disk I/O, swap-rate, PSI) is already captured at the same cadence in metric_sample (vmstat_pswpin/pswpout, memory_psi_full_avg10/60/300, block_device_sample) -- no gap there, confirmed by direct schema read.

title: Serving-stack tier for big-MoE: evaluate ktransformers / ik_llama.cpp / llama.cpp expert-offload tuning
description: Web-recon 2026-08-11: the ollama default is leaving MoE performance on the table. ktransformers (Tsinghua MADSys, SOSP'25 paper) keeps attention+KV on GPU and moves experts to CPU with optimized (AMX/AVX) kernels: 1.25-1.93x decode speedup over llama.cpp on quantized MoE, CUDA-graph scheduling, runs 671B-class MoE on one 24GB GPU + RAM (our 3080-10GB + 32GB RAM scales the same shape down). ik_llama.cpp offers tensor-level MoE offload (-ot exps=CPU patterns); mainline llama.cpp gained --n-cpu-moe / MoE-offload flags with a documented tuning guide (Doctor-Shotgun HF blog + gist). Value: (a) faster local-coder-moe/local-thinker/local-reasoner/gemma4:26b decode than ollama's automatic split; (b) possibly unlocks a bigger MoE tier (GLM-4.x-Air-class) at usable speed. Tasks: benchmark current ollama tok/s per MoE roster model as baseline; try llama.cpp-server with tuned expert-offload on qwen3-coder:30b; try ik_llama and ktransformers (intel AMX absent on i7-13700K — verify which kernels apply, AVX2 path); if a winner emerges, wire as an alternative litellm backend lane next to the ollama front door (registry-and-render per local-models.nix). Constraint: don't fork the serving estate casually — adopt only on a measured, meaningful win.
notes:
Sources: SOSP25 ktransformers paper (madsys.cs.tsinghua.edu.cn), HF blog Doctor-Shotgun llamacpp-moe-offload-guide, ik_llama hybrid docs, sglang issue #11425 (ktransformers integration effort).
2026-08-11 operator reframe: skip benchmark-first gating — implement directly (llama.cpp is already in the estate via the reranker service; adding a llama-server MoE lane with tuned --n-cpu-moe/-ot expert placement is low-risk and ollama keeps serving unchanged); benchmark falls out incidentally. WIDER PERF MENU recorded: (1) speculative decoding — llama.cpp draft-model support; qwen 0.5B drafts pair with qwen3-coder (ollama lacks this); (2) KV-cache quantization (q8_0 KV ≈ halves KV memory → double context or bigger model share on the 10GB card); (3) flash-attn + batch prompt processing defaults. HARDWARE ENABLERS (the real bigger-tier unlock): RAM is the binding constraint for MoE offload — 32GB caps total-params at the current ~19-20GB Q4 tier; 64-96GB DDR (i7-13700K platform supports 128GB — verify board/DIMM config) unlocks gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4 ~63GB, 5.1B active), GLM-4.x-Air-class (106B-A12B, Q4 ~58GB), Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (~42GB Q4) at usable tok/s because decode bandwidth scales with ACTIVE params (3-12B) while RAM only has to HOLD total params. A used RTX 3090 24GB is the parallel VRAM enabler (dense 30B fully resident + KV). ktransformers caveat: flagship AMX kernels are Xeon-only — on i7-13700K the AVX2 path applies; expected win smaller than paper numbers, ik_llama/llama.cpp offload flags may capture most of it.

title: Absorb RP-community text-hygiene + memory patterns into the agent/generation estate
description: Operator directive 2026-08-11, two absorptions: (1) SLOP-REGEX post-processing as a shared capability: port the ST Response-Processing phrase-strip pattern into a reusable component (scripts/sinnix-deslop or a shared filter lib + curated GPT-ism phrase inventory from community lists) applied at: yt-polisher translation output, agent-facing prose generation where applicable, html-report drafting lanes, and available as a lane post-processor in LiteLLM-adjacent tooling. Keep it structured (regex list as data file, versioned) per no-prose-grepping-for-ENFORCEMENT rule — this is output cleanup, not gating, which is fine. (2) MEMORY-PATTERN absorption: mine MemoryBooks (scene->structured entry), CharMemory (structured extraction->vector retrieval at generation), VectFox (event-extraction from filler: ~5 events per 100 sentences), LoreVault (summarize+search service) for the 8sf director state AND general agent-memory design (bd memories / context-handoff / polylogue-informed hermes memory seed in sinnix-z7v) — the specific steal: event-extraction before storage beats raw-log RAG, and keyword-triggered depth injection beats always-in-context.
notes: 2026-08-11 derived-data doctrine (operator asked for depth; applies to agent memory, 8sf state, lake, and is effectively sinex semantic-lane design language): TAXONOMY of derivations worth computing over raw — (1) EVENTS: {actor,action,object,time,salience} extracted from verbose streams; retrieval-sized, dedupable, timelineable — embedding whole replies averages filler into the vector, events fix the SNR at write time. (2) STATE REDUCTIONS: fold events into state-as-of-T with validity intervals (bitemporal: event-time vs record-time) — Tracker/ops-reducer pattern generalized. (3) HIERARCHICAL SUMMARIES: scene->chapter->arc / session->day->week, each linking back to raw; periodic re-derivation from raw to stop summary-of-summary drift. (4) CLAIMS with provenance: {claim, source-spans, confidence, ts} — deep-research verification shape doubling as personal-KG substrate. (5) UNIT-GRANULARITY EMBEDDINGS: proposition/event-level not doc-level (Dense-X 'propositions' finding), matryoshka-tiered, with deriver-version stamped for re-embedding policy. (6) SALIENCE SCORING at extraction + retrieval weighting recency x importance x relevance (Stanford generative-agents memory — the canonical design for 8sf). (7) ENTITY REGISTRIES: cross-source identity (speaker/face/username->person) enabling joins. (8) SUPERSESSION LINKS: new fact invalidates old via validity intervals — memory that updates, not accumulates. (9) STATISTICAL AGGREGATES: baselines/rhythms/changepoints (h8k). (10) RETRIEVAL REWRITES: QA-pair/question-form derivations of memories. DOCTRINES: re-derivability is the test (can't re-derive from raw => it's capture, not derivation); stamp every derivation with deriver model+prompt version; lazy-derive expensive tiers; raw remains sacred per lake rules.

title: RP-community knowledge harvest: samplers, finetune scene, context-engineering practice, frontend evaluation

2026-08-11 web-recon — SEMANTIC-LAYER/MEMORY prior art (evaluate before building item 8's store): agent-memory frameworks matured into a real category: Graphiti/Zep (TEMPORAL knowledge graph — bitemporal edges align exactly with the uou derived-data doctrine's bitemporal state-reductions), cognee (graph+vector hybrid, ECL pipeline, 14 retrieval modes, self-hostable), mem0 (three-tier user/session/agent scopes), Letta (MemGPT lineage, agent-managed memory tiers — framework not layer). None are lake-native; the likely pattern is stealing Graphiti's temporal-edge schema + cognee's graph+vector split over OUR duckdb/parquet substrate rather than adopting a framework. Also Khoj (self-hosted 'second brain': RAG over notes + custom agents + scheduled automations + deep research) — closest packaged analogue to the estate's ambitions; evaluate its UX patterns (Obsidian/editor integration, automation scheduling), not its storage. Vector-store shortlist for item 8 unchanged by search outage: LanceDB (columnar, file-based — /realm-friendly), sqlite-vec (embeds in existing sqlite products), usearch (library-grade), qdrant (server-grade).
2026-08-11 positioning vs Polylogue (operator ask): NOT competitors — different layers. Polylogue is the RAW ARCHIVAL SUBSTRATE for AI-session history (append-only ingestion of Claude/Codex/ChatGPT sessions, markdown+sqlite, search over what was SAID). Memory frameworks (Graphiti/Zep, cognee, mem0, Letta) are OPERATIONAL memory: derived, mutable, retrieval-optimized state consulted at inference time (entities, facts, temporal edges, supersession). The estate's correct shape: polylogue+lake stay the immutable evidence plane; a DERIVED temporal-KG layer (Graphiti's bitemporal edge schema: valid-from/valid-to + ingested-at — matches the uou doctrine's bitemporal state-reductions and supersession-links classes) is materialized FROM polylogue/lynchpin/captures by lynchpin jobs, re-derivable and versioned; agents query the derived layer, cite back to raw. Adopting Letta/mem0 wholesale would create a second, non-lake-native store of truth — rejected. Khoj: overlapping UX (RAG over notes, agents, scheduled automations, editor integrations) but storage-opinionated; read for UX patterns only. Note bd's own 'bd remember' + beads memories already cover the small-scale agent-memory slot for tracker-adjacent facts.
2026-08-11 operator correction ACCEPTED: bitemporality is already estate doctrine, not a Graphiti import — sinex models occurrence-time vs recorded/ingest-time on events (the replay-later doctrine depends on it), and polylogue distinguishes session-time vs ingestion analogously. Graphiti's only delta is applying that discipline at the DERIVED-FACT level (per-edge valid_from/valid_to/invalidated_at on knowledge-graph edges). Design rule: the derived temporal-KG layer adopts SINEX's existing time-field naming/conventions so one bitemporal vocabulary spans raw events and derived facts; Graphiti is a schema reference only.

title: Vocal training & speech-analysis toolkit: pronunciation feedback, pitch/prosody analysis, language learning loops
description: Operator interest 2026-08-11: vocal training of all kinds incl. programmatic, language learning, feedback schemes, analysis. Toolkit design: (1) ANALYSIS SUBSTRATE — parselmouth (Praat as a Python library: formants, F0, jitter/shimmer/HNR = voice-quality + articulation measurement, fully programmatic); CREPE/pYIN for high-res pitch (singing/intonation training); (2) PRONUNCIATION FEEDBACK — Montreal Forced Aligner (phoneme-level alignment) + wav2vec2-phoneme/allosaurus (universal phoneme recognition) -> GOP (goodness-of-pronunciation) scoring per phoneme against target language; visualize weak phonemes over time; (3) REFERENCE GENERATION — TTS trio produces native-speaker reference audio of ANY practice sentence (Fish for Polish/multilingual) -> shadowing loops with DTW prosody-contour comparison (your F0/timing vs reference, scored); (4) the clever one: SELF-ACCENT FEEDBACK — voice conversion (RVC/Seed-VC) renders a native-accented version of YOUR OWN voice saying the target sentence = hear yourself-as-corrected (research-grade accent-conversion idea, practically approximable today); (5) singing: range/intonation tracking vs reference via pitch curves. All local, all composable with the nm7 capture (practice sessions auto-recorded and scored). Commercial reference point: Azure Pronunciation Assessment is the API gold standard (phoneme-level scores) — local GOP pipeline is the open equivalent.
notes:
2026-08-11 web-recon prior-art anchors: GVPT (arXiv 2505.00750 — guided visual pitch tracking with three guidance styles; the exercise-UI shape), TruVox (web-based structured pitch training, transgender-voice provenance but generally applicable exercise design), 30-year singing-assessment survey (arXiv 2601.12153 — the field map: intonation/rhythm scoring methods), automatic singing-mistake detection for pedagogy (arXiv 2602.06917). Parselmouth substrate plan unchanged; these give exercise design + scoring method references so we don't reinvent assessment.
2026-08-11 design deepening (operator ask — rapid feedback + atomic leverage skills): FEEDBACK SCHEMES, all local-realtime-capable: (a) <100ms scrolling pitch trace with target lane (GVPT's guidance styles); (b) live F1/F2 formant-space dot with target regions (vowel placement made visible — parselmouth); (c) per-rep score via pitch-contour DTW against reference (prosody/intonation imitation); (d) spectrogram overlay self-vs-reference; (e) ASR-confidence / phoneme-posterior as pronunciation score (whisper logprobs or a GOP pipeline); (f) sustained-phonation dashboard (jitter/shimmer/HNR + SPL stability). ATOMIC SKILLS with transfer leverage, each trainable alone: (1) pitch matching (foundation for everything melodic+prosodic); (2) interval production; (3) breath support / sustained phonation stability (carries speech AND singing); (4) vowel formant placement (accent, clarity, resonance); (5) onset control (glottal/breathy/balanced); (6) vibrato rate-depth control (isolatable oscillation skill); (7) resonance/twang (spectral-tilt target); (8) rhythm reproduction (tap + vocal); (9) prosody contour imitation (the 8sf sarcasm-drill production side — same DTW machinery); (10) minimal-pair perception (auto-generated via TTS pairs, language learning); (11) shadowing latency (speech-to-speech echo delay as a metric). Curriculum shape: perception before production per skill; personal-baseline stats per the 8sf philosophy.

title: Content gates: evaluate Presidio + Llama-Guard for publication egress and lake pipelines
description: Operator interest 2026-08-11: could safety/PII models sensibly gate agent commits? Llama-Guard-3-1B adds content-policy labels — relevant mainly for lake->training pipelines, not commits. Caution per repo doctrine: gates must stay advisory/structured, judgment remains the committer's; benchmark false-positive rate on real diffs before any enforcement.
notes:
2026-08-11 LANDSCAPE EXPANSION + gate architecture (operator: wire ~all public-repo egress):
GUARD MODELS (verified current 2026-08): Llama-Guard family (3-1B latency tier / 3-8B quality tier / 4-12B multimodal, MLCommons hazard taxonomy — 4 and ShieldGemma-2 are NOT ollama-servable, plan llama.cpp/vllm); ShieldGemma 1 (2B/9B/27B policy-specific) + ShieldGemma 2 (4B image safety); IBM Granite Guardian 3.3 (8B/5B — adds prompt-injection + RAG-hallucination axes beyond harm; 5B = balanced default); AI2 WildGuard 7B (highest benign-set precision = least over-blocking — the right temperament for a personal egress gate); NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails (framework, not model). Small classics: distilbert-nsfw-text, Detoxify, KoalaAI/Text-Moderation. PII: Presidio (this bead's original scope) + secrets scanners gitleaks/trufflehog as the mechanical tier.
KEYWORD/PHRASE DICTS (operator addition — the missed layer): LDNOOBW multilingual obscenity lists (the corpus-filtering classic), Surge AI profanity list (multilingual), HurtLex (multilingual hurtful-term lexicon), slur lists, UT1/oisd/hagezi URL-category lists (already in w9l); PLUS a PERSONAL TRIPWIRE DICT — project codenames, usernames, community names, dataset and model names (motivated by a 2026-08-11 near-miss that manual review caught; the dict would have tripped it mechanically before export).
FALSE-POSITIVE DOCTRINE (operator concern: profanity/terms in non-NSFW contexts — Scunthorpe problem): dicts are HIGH-RECALL TRIPWIRES, never verdicts. Tiered gate: T0 mechanical (secrets scanners, path shapes — auto-BLOCK, only tier allowed to block); T1 dict/regex flag (cheap, every commit); T2 classifier pass over flagged+sampled hunks (WildGuard for precision, Granite-5B for breadth, distilbert-nsfw/Detoxify as light axes); T3 local LLM adjudication of tripped spans WITH surrounding context (resolves quoted-profanity/technical-term cases) -> REVIEW QUEUE for the committer, never auto-reject. This preserves the CLAUDE.md rule that no script judges content — the gate assists the committer's review, it does not replace it; it is also NOT process-invariant-by-NLP-grep (the anti-pattern rule) because it flags for judgment rather than enforcing.
WIRE POINTS (priority order): (1) beads export path — gate .beads/issues.jsonl content before commit (the proven near-miss vector); (2) pre-push hook on all public repos (sinnix/sinex/polylogue/lynchpin) over the outgoing diff; (3) CI second layer (public behavioral checks already exist — add content tripwire job); (4) later: agent-gateway/artifact egress.
DATA PLACEMENT (operator decision): dicts/lists/eval datasets live in the LAKE not the repo — /realm/media/corpora/content-lists/ (reference material per the new corpora/ member), guard model weights /realm/media/model per convention; repos hold only pointers + gate config.
2026-08-11 incident addendum: a tracker checkpoint commit MESSAGE briefly leaked repo-boundary metadata to the public repo and required a history rewrite (GitHub events API retains old push events for a while — accepted residual; full purge needs a GitHub support request). Rules for the gate hardened by this: (1) T1 tripwire must scan COMMIT MESSAGES and PR/issue bodies, not just diff content — metadata channels are publication surfaces; (2) any cross-tracker pointer or process note in public carriers must be phrased neutrally (plain issue-id references, no characterization of what moved or why); (3) fixes to leaked-metadata commits are history REWRITES from the parent, never sanitization follow-ups — a follow-up leaves the leak reachable in history.

title: Finetune + mech-interp program over the local model estate (EOT, grammars-from-datasets, per-purpose adapters)
description: Operator direction 2026-08-11: leverage owned datasets (atuin, polylogue, captures) for domain finetunes across the estate, starting with command-dictation EOT (LiveKit turn-detector recipe; synth audio via TTS reading atuin commands; LoRA minutes-scale on 3080). Principles decided: per-purpose adapters over one model (LoRA sidesteps catastrophic forgetting — base stays frozen, adapters swap; many small experts is the right shape and cheap). Dynamic grammars: generate GBNF command grammars FROM live context (PATH bins, current repo's scripts, hyprland dispatchers) — an LLM managing grammar/adapter selection at runtime; finetuning the manager itself is the stretch goal (feasible on-machine at <=8B QLoRA; bigger off-machine). Research tasks: command-dictation prior art (whisper-typing/voice-coding projects), full voice-control setup surveys. Mech-interp tie-in: interp-lab (transformer-lens/SAE) already installed — probe/visualize the small finetuned models (135M EOT is an ideal interp subject), Gemma Scope SAEs for the gemma tiers.
notes:
2026-08-11k: base-model lane additions — Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base + Qwen2.5-7B-base into local roster; LOOM-CLASS UI for base-model interaction (operator req): socketteer/loom or obsidian-loom pointed at the LiteLLM-compatible endpoint — tree-branching high-n exploration UI, the right interface for the 8sf director sampling harness and for base-model play generally. OLMo-2 auditability exercise: Dolma corpus is greppable — directly MEASURE domain representation (e.g. NSFW/dating discourse) in training data instead of guessing; unique to OLMo; also intermediate checkpoints -> training-dynamics interp studies.
2026-08-11m: checkpoint-interp PRIOR ART recorded — Pythia (EleutherAI) is the canonical public checkpoint suite (154 checkpoints, 70M-12B, dozens of published training-dynamics papers) and Timaeus/devinterp does singular-learning-theory phase-transition analysis publicly; the Gwern-flavored study is NOT novel science — local value = hands-on learning, OLMo-2's newer/bigger models (32B vs Pythia's 12B ceiling) + measurable corpus, and PERSONAL questions (when does capability X my use cares about emerge). Position the project as replication-plus-extension, start from Pythia notebooks.
2026-08-11n BASE-MODEL FINETUNING feasibility (operator: own-reddit-corpus model): LOCAL on the 3080/10GB — QLoRA (4-bit base + LoRA) trains 7-8B dense comfortably (unsloth-class stack fits 7B in ~6-8GB; 14B marginal at short context); full finetuning is out (optimizer states need 8x+ the VRAM). Personal reddit corpus (~1M tokens class from the lake export) x few epochs = minutes-to-an-hour locally. MoE (Qwen3-30B-A3B): NOT locally trainable despite 3B-active — ALL expert weights participate in backprop (~16-18GB at 4-bit weights alone) and RAM-offload training is impractically slow -> cloud. CLOUD COSTS: A100-80GB rents ~$1.3-1.8/hr (RunPod/Vast class); 30B QLoRA over a personal corpus = hour-scale = single-digit dollars; even 70B QLoRA fits one A100 = <$10 per experiment. DESIGN for the reddit-ghost: (context,reply) pairs (export has permalinks; parent text via dumps/API) rather than bare continuation; mix ~10-20% general data against style-collapse; LoRA adapter = forgetting-proof + swappable per the established many-small-adapters principle; evaluate by blinded self-vs-model discrimination. Ties 8sf (a self-simulator is the ultimate personal-distribution probe) and the loom UI for sampling it.
2026-08-11: further dataset-map material tracked in stashbox-5vd.
2026-08-11 LOW-DISTORTION REAL-DYAD CORPORA map (complementary corpora; see also stashbox-5vd): (1) Wikipedia TALK PAGES (official dumps) — real negotiation-through-text at scale, argument/consensus dynamics, zero performative-broadcast incentive; (2) Usenet archives — dialogic threading from the pre-performative web; (3) IRC logs (ubuntu-irc et al public logs) — synchronous informal group dyads; (4) mailing lists (LKML etc.) — technical negotiation/conflict, fully public; (5) SPOKEN dyad gold: Switchboard/Fisher/CALLHOME (LDC-licensed telephone conversations — THE spontaneous-speech classics), CANDOR corpus (large modern recorded video conversations w/ transcripts, research access) — real turn-taking/backchannel/EOT statistics for mke/8sf; (6) AMI/ICSI meeting corpora — real multiparty meetings; (7) negotiation datasets: CaSiNo, Deal-or-No-Deal (crowdsourced but genuinely adversarial dyads); (8) AnnoMI (motivational-interviewing transcripts — clinical-conversation dynamics, open); court transcripts (adversarial dialogue under oath, public record); (9) historical published correspondence collections (long-horizon dyads); (10) game/MMO chat research corpora. Distortion profiles differ but all are INTERACTION records not broadcast performance — the axis that makes the RP-forum dyad corpus valuable. EOT/turn-taking finetunes (mke) should draw on 5-6; director conversational statistics on 1/5/7/8.
2026-08-11 web-recon: (1) DYNAMIC-GRAMMARS PRIOR ART — XGrammar-2 (arXiv 2601.04426) is literally 'efficient dynamic structured generation for agentic LLMs' (pushdown-automata engine, 14x JSON / 80x CFG speedups vs engines) — read before building the grammar-manager; llama.cpp GBNF stays the local serving path but XGrammar-2's dynamic-grammar API is the design reference; Guidance still wins TPOT in some benchmarks (arXiv 2501.10868). (2) NOVEL-ARCH tier for the base-model/interp interests: diffusion LLMs went production 2026 — LLaDA 2.0 (100B-scale, BERT-like bidirectional, NO KV cache — long-context memory advantage), LLaDA-MoE, Dream-Coder 7B (open diffusion code model — grabbable), Mercury 2 (commercial, 1000+ tok/s). Grab Dream-Coder-7B + a small LLaDA for interp studies (attention-sinks-in-dLLMs already a paper thread) and parallel-infill experiments; block-diffusion (32-token blocks) is the emerging standard shape.
2026-08-11 XGrammar-2 read (arXiv 2601.04426, ACM CAIS'26): the agentic problem is output structure varying ACROSS and WITHIN requests. Mechanisms: TagDispatch (tags in the stream trigger grammar switching mid-generation — exactly the runtime grammar-manager shape this bead planned), cross-grammar substructure cache (new grammars reuse compiled fragments — cheap per-context grammar generation), Earley-based adaptive token-mask cache, JIT compilation, repetition-state compression; >6x faster grammar compilation, near-zero serving overhead. Implication for us: dynamic grammars-from-context are a SOLVED ENGINE problem in the vllm/sglang lineage; llama.cpp's GBNF remains static-per-request — so the grammar-heavy lanes (command dictation, mechanics-registrar) may justify a vllm/sglang-class endpoint with xgrammar rather than teaching llama.cpp dynamic switching. The 09q serving-lane work should keep this consumer in mind.
2026-08-11 DIFFUSION-LM lane (operator: want): non-dominated open set — LLaDA-8B Base+Instruct (the original, TRUE BASE EXISTS — bidirectional infilling base is a novel loom/population-sampling toy: conditions on BOTH sides of a span, which AR bases cannot), Dream-7B base+instruct (Qwen2.5-initialized, strong small dLLM), Dream-Coder-7B (open diffusion code model), LLaDA-MoE (~7B-A1B class, diffusion+MoE), LLaDA 2.0 (100B-scale — API/big-RAM only). Proprietary: Mercury 2 (Inception, 1000+ tok/s, API), Gemini Diffusion (Google, experimental/waitlist). DIFFUSION EMBEDDINGS confirmed real: EMNLP 2025 'Diffusion vs. AR LMs: A Text Embedding Perspective' — bidirectional attention gives +20% long-document retrieval, +8% reasoning-intensive retrieval vs LLM embedders; DiffRetriever (arXiv 2605.07210) continues the line. Watch for released checkpoints; would slot into the lake retrieval stack above the current qwen3/jina tier for long docs. Interp angle: no KV cache + bidirectional = different attention-sink phenomenology (arXiv 2510.15731) — fresh interp-lab subject.
2026-08-11 diffusion addenda: Mercury 2 pricing (verified): Inception direct API $0.15/M in, $0.35/M out; via OpenRouter ~$0.25/$0.75 (released 2026-03-04). THE CATCH (why diffusion isn't frontier yet, recorded honestly): (1) quality-per-training-FLOP at frontier scale unproven — every frontier lab's data/RLHF/eval pipeline is AR-native, so dLLMs compete against a decade of AR-specific optimization; (2) each denoising step recomputes full bidirectional attention over the WHOLE sequence — compute per token grows with sequence length worse than cached AR, so the throughput win inverts at long contexts (the no-KV-cache memory win is real, the compute bill moves elsewhere); (3) no natural token-level logprobs/exact likelihood — RLHF/RLVR tooling, sampling controls (temperature/logit-bias ecosystems), and eval harnesses all need rework; (4) streaming UX is block-wise, not token-wise; (5) serving/quantization/finetuning ecosystem years behind (llama.cpp cannot run them; HF transformers or bespoke engines only); (6) instruction-following/reasoning parity only recently claimed (Mercury 2) and not independently replicated broadly. For EMBEDDINGS none of 1-4 apply — that's why diffusion embedders already win on long-doc retrieval and the main blocker is checkpoint availability.

title: Calibrate quota attribution and model advice in Lynchpin
description: Use normalized provider windows, Sinnix job intervals, Polylogue token evidence, and task outcomes to estimate quota-equivalent consumption and produce advisory model and effort choices. Keep this asynchronous in Lynchpin and outside the live reducer request path.
design: Implement in /realm/project/sinity-lynchpin after quota coverage and agent identity are stable. Partition by provider, account hash, and plan epoch. Fit a non-negative robust model over quota deltas and overlapping job features: uncached input, cache reads and writes, output, reasoning, tool duration, and wall time. Preserve attributed and unattributed quota, coverage, confidence intervals, residuals, and change points. Build empirical workload classes from Beads and verified job outcomes, then publish a dated advisory product with expected quota use, duration, verification rate, remaining equivalent tasks, and binding window. The live reducer only reads the latest materialized product. Automatic routing is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic overlapping jobs recover known coefficients within a stated interval; real products expose coverage and residuals; plan changes create separate epochs; low-coverage windows produce no confident advice; workload classes link to Beads and verified outcomes; advisory rankings include quota, duration, quality evidence, and binding window; Lynchpin materialization and graph tests pass; no live request invokes DuckDB or model fitting.

title: Decide and prove one Hyprland plugin strategy
description: Compare version-locked Hyprland flake plugins, vendored plugin builds, and selecting no plugin. Measure ABI compatibility, cache and rebuild cost, update coupling, and recovery path. Select at most one of hyprsplit, hyprscrolling, or hyprexpo for an end-to-end proof if evidence supports plugins.
design: Produce a decision record before code. Inspect current Hyprland and nixpkgs pins and each candidate plugin's matching revision requirements. Estimate closure and rebuild cost with no live activation. Select the lowest-risk strategy, then attempt one plugin in an isolated branch with a rollback command prepared. If ABI or cache evidence is poor, reject plugins explicitly. Do not test multiple plugins live in one session.
acceptance_criteria: A decision record cites current pins and build evidence; rejected options have concrete reasons; either one plugin builds, loads, and survives reload on the live host, or plugins are explicitly rejected without leaving partial wiring.
notes: Decision: reject hyprsplit, hyprscrolling, and hyprexpo for the current desktop. Evidence: live Hyprland is 0.55.4 at commit a0136d8c04687bb36eb8a28eb9d1ff92aea99704; flake.lock pins nixpkgs e4bae1bd10c9c57b2cf517953ab70060a828ee6f; the pinned nixpkgs plugin definitions are hyprsplit 0.52.1 and upstream hyprscrolling/hyprexpo 0.52.0. The existing source decision record at modules/features/desktop/hyprland/default.nix:173-177 was introduced in c83141a and records the prior hyprexpo compile failure due to missing HookSystemManager.hpp, proving the ABI mismatch. No plugin package exists in the current system closure and no plugin wiring exists in the active tree. Rejected options: hyprexpo, because the recorded build failure is exact; hyprscrolling, because it shares the same out-of-sync upstream plugin release family and Hyprland ABI; hyprsplit, because its separate 0.52.1 release is also versioned against the older plugin API and has no compatible pinned Hyprland-flake revision. Selected strategy: no Hyprland plugin. Verification: hyprctl version; source and flake.lock inspection; live config contains no plugin load entries. No switch was required because the deployed no-plugin state is unchanged. No partial wiring or rollback residue was introduced. The shared heavy-work lease prevented a fresh derivation build probe, so the decision relies on the prior recorded compiler failure plus current pin evidence.
close_reason: Rejected all candidate Hyprland plugins on recorded ABI failure and current pin evidence; retained the deployed no-plugin strategy with no partial wiring.

title: Secrets egress guard: scan outward-bound content before publish

design: Guard only explicit outward publication commands using structured hook events. Never print matched secret bytes; report detector, source path or argument index, and remediation. Treat screenshots and binary artifacts through metadata or dedicated image privacy checks, not text decoding. Permit an explicit per-invocation operator override that is recorded without the payload. Golden fixtures cover a fake token, clean technical text, binary input, oversized input, and non-public commands.
acceptance_criteria: A fake credential in a file argument and request body is denied without printing the match. Clean text, binary, oversized, non-public, and explicit-override fixtures follow the documented policy. A benchmark records median and p95 clean-path overhead against a predeclared budget before the hook is enabled. Supported detectors and blind spots are documented.

For unsupported events, document manual discipline in the common instructions and mark the parity matrix manual. Do not simulate unsupported hooks with terminal scraping. Use the hooks harness for each portable guard and inspect generated Codex hooks.json after switch. The deliverable is a versioned parity table plus implementations only where the client exposes sufficient structured input.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned matrix lists every Claude guard and its Codex state as enforced, unsupported, or manual with evidence from current client capabilities. Equivalent guards share one helper and have client-specific golden fixtures. Unsupported rules use no terminal scraping. Generated Codex configuration and shared instructions match the matrix after switch.

title: memory-staleness routine: monthly audit of agent memory files

design: Discover actual agent memory files from configured roots rather than assuming MEMORY.md exists everywhere. Parse entries conservatively and emit a proposal report with file, line, age, referenced path status, and evidence of contradiction. Absolute dates and dead paths are mechanical signals; semantic contradiction requires review and must not be auto-edited. Run monthly as a read-only user timer and retain bounded reports. title: Fleet vacuity sampling: SubagentStop -> judge verdicts on suspicious outputs
description: SubagentStop hook samples completed agents (all whose last message is very short / all-green / citation-free, plus N% random) and enqueues judge (gg7) verdicts: does this output evidence real work? Results into the dispatch ledger (polylogue-u49yr). Converts the anti-vacuity contract into measurement.
design: Do not launch a judge synchronously from SubagentStop. The hook emits a bounded completion candidate into the existing agent audit or attention event stream and returns immediately. A background worker applies deterministic sampling metadata: explicit suspicious signals from structured output facts plus a configurable random rate. It calls claude-judge with a closed schema and records verdict, evidence, refutation attempt, model, cost, and source session ID in the dispatch ledger. Prompt text and transcript content are referenced by bounded artifact handles. Sampling policy is versioned so rates are comparable. Human false-positive review is a separate labeled verdict, not edited prose.
acceptance_criteria: SubagentStop returns within its hook timeout while a candidate is queued; duplicate completion events deduplicate by session and terminal event ID; configured deterministic and random samples are reproducible from policy version and seed; judge receipts validate and join the dispatch ledger; a week report includes sampled denominator, verdict distribution, cost, and reviewed false-positive rate.

title: borg freshness/queue alarm fires during planned integrity check
description: borgbackup-status flags archive_freshness ok:false and snapshot_queue ok:false while borgbackup-check.service legitimately holds the repo for many hours (observed 2026-08-02: check running 14h, drains correctly skipping with 'Another Borg operation is active', 35 realm snapshots queued, freshness age 17h > 6h budget). The pause is by design; the alarm is noise. Make the status check aware of an active borgbackup-check invocation: either suppress freshness/queue alarms while the check runs (and alarm instead on check runtime exceeding its own budget), or raise the freshness budget to cover the check window.
design: Model planned integrity work as a typed backup state, not an alert suppression string. Extend the backup status event schema with operation kind, run ID, expected affected jobs, start, deadline, and state. Freshness evaluation suppresses only the jobs explicitly covered by an active, unexpired integrity run and reports maintenance rather than healthy. A failed or overdue integrity run becomes red. Derive state from the integrity unit and its receipt, never from process-name matching. Historical freshness remains visible.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture integrity run changes only covered jobs from stale to maintenance; unrelated stale jobs remain red; expired, failed, and missing receipts become red; normal freshness resumes after completion; notifications transition once per state change and the status snapshot exposes maintenance with run ID and deadline.
notes: Implementation checkpoint 2026-08-07: modules/backup.nix now records a typed integrity receipt at /persist/root/.cache/borg-drain/integrity-check.json with operation_kind, run_id, expected_jobs, start_epoch, deadline_epoch, state, and updated_at. borgbackup-check.service writes running before repository checks and completed or failed on exit. borgbackup-status.service reads only the receipt, marks covered stale archive jobs maintenance while the deadline is valid, leaves unrelated stale jobs red, and marks expired, failed, or missing receipts red. Snapshot and archive history remain visible. It emits notification_transition JSONL records only when a label state changes, with run ID and deadline, and the archive snapshot includes state, run_id, and deadline_epoch. Added flake/tests/backup.nix heavy fixture covering covered maintenance, unrelated stale jobs, repeated-poll transition suppression, expired, failed, missing, and completed receipt states. Verification: sinnix-heavy-lease --wait-seconds 300 -- nix develop --command nix run .#check-heavy reached and passed heavyChecks.x86_64-linux.backup-status-integrity-state-runtime; the same suite later stopped at the unrelated pre-existing dev-agent-tools-runtime failure. Applied live with sinnix-heavy-lease --wait-seconds 300 -- nix develop --command switch. Live checks: nixos-version --configuration-revision reported 75babf93bf773b76008471b162118aaf5db9ce6f-dirty; generated borgbackup-check and borgbackup-status units contain the receipt logic; systemctl start --wait borgbackup-status.service emitted archive_freshness red records with message integrity check receipt is missing and exited nonzero as required. Deliberately excluded: no process-name matching, no historical freshness deletion, no Borg check execution or receipt fabrication during live verification. Follow-up: run the next scheduled integrity check and confirm a real running/completed receipt transitions the live status back through maintenance to healthy.
close_reason: Typed integrity receipts and scoped maintenance status are deployed. Heavy fixture and live unit verification cover all acceptance criteria; missing receipt is red in the live status run, and the broader suite has an unrelated dev-agent-tools-runtime baseline failure.

title: Config streamlining: prune default-valued settings, convert protective defaults into eval assertions
description: Operator-requested sweep (2026-07-10): go through the module tree and (a) DELETE settings explicitly set to their upstream-default values (noise that implies deliberateness where none exists — e.g. zramSwap.algorithm zstd IS the NixOS default as of 25.05+, several systemd timerConfig.Persistent=false spellings match defaults), (b) settings that merely might-as-well-be defaults: drop unless a comment earns them, and (c) the interesting class — settings kept AT default deliberately because changing them broke things (e.g. 'do not use nix profile', 'zramSwap disabled' historically, boot.tmp choices): these are invariants wearing config clothing, and belong as ASSERTIONS with failure-mode documentation instead of passive comments. Pattern: eval-time assertions in the module (assertion = config.foo == default; message = what went wrong when it was set otherwise + incident date) or hermetic checks in flake/tests-runtime.nix via mkFeatureTest, so a future edit that flips them gets an immediate, self-explaining failure instead of a re-lived incident. Method: for each module, diff effective values against nixos option defaults (nixos-option or options.json from the system closure) rather than guessing; batch by module; keep the no-alias rule (no transition shims).
design: Treat this as a parent audit split by module taxonomy. Children own infrastructure and profiles, features, and services. Each child reads evaluated option defaults from the current pinned NixOS option metadata, classifies explicit values as redundant, explanatory, or invariant, and changes one coherent module cluster. Delete redundant values, retain values whose explicitness communicates a real choice, and encode only behaviorally valuable invariants as assertions or runtime checks. Do not add tests that merely forbid old text. Each child runs focused checks and the parent runs one final switch after all merges.
acceptance_criteria:
- a full-module-tree pass recorded: list of removed default-valued settings, list of kept-with-comment, list converted to assertions
- at least the known invariant class (rebuild containment, dotfiles-writable settings.json, persistence-or-wiped, nodatacow-on-DB-subvols) expressed as assertions/tests with incident-dated messages
- check tier still green; switch applied
notes:
Handoff reconciliation 2026-08-07: gateway option cleanup belongs only after the closed sinnix-056 migration/deletion evidence and must not become an independent gateway refactor. Audit effective defaults and invariants in the existing module taxonomy.

- ow0.2 feature defaults: satisfied. Complete feature matrix recorded; zero deletions claimed without pinned evidence; default-on factory and dotfile ownership preserved; CLI and Noctalia focused checks passed.
- ow0.3 service defaults: satisfied. Complete service-family matrix and factory exceptions recorded; runtime-surface policy and persistence declarations were preserved; focused service check passed.
- ow0.4 Prime capability/lifecycle truth: satisfied. Derived sinnix-capability-manifest-v1 joins source declarations, runtime inventory, live systemd state, generation drift, path references, explicit unknowns, and dormant Ethereal. Focused fixture and switch passed.

Parent classifications: removed default-valued settings are documented as zero where no safe candidate had pinned upstream-default evidence; kept-with-policy values are classified in the child matrices; converted invariants are the incident-dated assertions/checks from ow0.1. The latest live generation is acb2266 and the default check was invoked but its aggregate result was not captured by the command wrapper, so repository-wide green is not claimed. No gateway refactor, host-role migration, capability deletion, capture opt-out, or local-agent restriction was introduced.

title: environmentAllowList implies an env boundary that scope mode does not enforce (and the list is stale)
description: sinnix-scope builds --setenv args from runtimeDefaults.environmentAllowList, but it launches via 'systemd-run --scope', where the command runs as a child of the caller and inherits the FULL environment — the allowlist filters nothing (verified by reading scripts/sinnix-scope:166-202 + systemd-run scope semantics). Consequences: (1) the list is dead weight that misleads readers into thinking an env boundary exists; (2) it is dangerously incomplete if anyone ever switches to service mode — it lacks ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/ANTHROPIC_MODEL/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY/LITELLM_LOCAL_KEY/CONTEXT7_API_KEY/SINNIX_CLAUDE_PROFILE/SINNIX_CODEX_PROFILE, so claude-local/claude-deepseek would silently fall back to the real Anthropic backend and codex hook profile-gating would misfire. Fix: either delete the allowlist + --setenv plumbing and document scope-inheritance at the call site, or (if a real boundary is wanted) switch to service-mode launches and complete the list. Decide once; do not leave the phantom boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Either allowlist plumbing removed with an inheritance comment, or service-mode launch with a complete verified list (claude-local reaches LiteLLM through the scope)
close_reason: Deleted the phantom --setenv plumbing and environmentAllowList data table entirely (scripts/sinnix-scope, flake/data/runtime-defaults.nix) rather than build out a complete allowlist for a boundary systemd-run --scope can't enforce. Documented scope-inheritance explicitly in-script. Verified live: /etc/sinnix/runtime-inventory.json no longer has an environmentAllowList key.

title: Oracle digests are wiped every reboot — persist ~/.local/share/oracle
description: modules/services/oracle.nix writes daily digests to %h/.local/share/oracle (timer Persistent=true), but that path is not in sinnix.persistence.home.directories — the whole digest archive is destroyed on every boot (impermanence wipes @). Today's digest regenerates on the next timer fire but history is unrecoverable, and the advice-fate feedback loop needs past digests. Fix: colocate a persistence declaration in oracle.nix per the repo convention (persistence declared next to the owning module). Sweep result for context: all other /var/lib and ~/.local state writers check out (open-webui persisted in-module, litellm documented stateless, sinnix-browser reseeds by design).
acceptance_criteria: ~/.local/share/oracle survives reboot; declaration lives in oracle.nix
close_reason: Added sinnix.persistence.home.directories = [ ".local/share/oracle" ]; inside oracle.nix's configFn (gated by cfg.enable like the rest of the module, per repo convention).

title: sshd.socket is a listen-less stub unit created only to set Slice
description: networking.nix:113 sets systemd.sockets.sshd.socketConfig.Slice, but services.openssh.startWhenNeeded is false so NixOS never defines a real sshd.socket — the config MATERIALIZES a stub unit with a [Socket] section containing only Slice= and no ListenStream (verified live: systemctl cat sshd.socket). close_reason: Deleted the systemd.sockets.sshd stub block (networking.nix) and the sshd-socket baseSurfaces entry (runtime-defaults.nix). Verified live: systemctl cat sshd.socket now reports no unit.

title: On-demand local AI services via socket activation
description: ollama/koboldcpp/comfyui/whisper/tts/open-webui are enable=true + autoStart=false + manual systemctl start — friction and bookkeeping. Add socket-activation (systemd .socket units on :11434/:5001/:8188/:8090/:8000, or a small proxy-activate unit for services without native sd_listen support) so the first request cold-starts the service; add idle-timeout stop (RuntimeMaxSec or an idle-checker) to free VRAM/RAM. Removes the autoStart dimension for the AI tier and makes claude-local/codex-local work from cold. Note GPU services: serialize wake so two models don't race for VRAM (koboldcpp + ollama).
design: Use systemd socket proxy activation for HTTP services that cannot consume LISTEN_FDS. Each public loopback socket retains the documented port; the backend moves to a private loopback port, and systemd-socket-proxyd connects to it with service ordering and an idle exit timeout. Services with native socket activation may bind the socket directly. Declare local-AI activation metadata once on each service surface. For mutually exclusive large LLM backends, generate pairwise Conflicts from one exclusiveResource group so systemd serializes transitions; do not build a second scheduler. Preserve dependent chains such as LiteLLM to Ollama. Implement one CPU service and one GPU service first, prove cold start and idle stop, then migrate the rest. Stop if a protocol uses long-lived connections that make proxy idle detection unsafe and record a service-specific design.
acceptance_criteria: A stopped CPU and GPU service cold-start through their documented ports; backend ports are not externally exposed; idle timeout frees the service and GPU memory after clients disconnect; two services in the exclusive GPU group cannot remain active simultaneously; dependent LiteLLM or Open WebUI flow works from cold; runtime inventory reports activation and exclusivity metadata; long-lived protocol exceptions are explicitly documented.
notes:
Held after source and live-shape inspection. Current Ollama, LiteLLM, Whisper, KoboldCpp, ComfyUI, and TTS services bind their public loopback ports directly; no existing socket-activation or GPU-exclusivity helper is present. Implementing this safely requires a designed proxy/backend port contract, runtime inventory activation metadata, idle-stop semantics, and live cold-start/long-lived protocol proof. No c32 files changed. Revisit after an explicit design slice or operator-approved service migration.
Corrected handoff reconciliation 2026-08-07: retain the full Prime backend set and broad local-AI capability. Implement shared lifecycle/readiness/failure/idle-stop and GPU/VRAM admission only after current service protocols are verified; native socket activation only where supported, otherwise use a truthful API/command activation path. Record backend identity, cold-start, request activity, idle-stop, and lifecycle evidence in existing runtime inventory and Sinex paths. Do not consolidate to one backend or delete a low-use capability. Current source/live inspection found direct public loopback binds and no reusable activation/exclusivity helper, so this remains a design-gated implementation.
Implemented the corrected handoff's viable local-AI activation slice. Files: modules/services/ai-control.nix adds loopback systemd socket proxies for Ollama 11434->11435, KoboldCpp 5001->5002, and LiteLLM 4000->4001 with 30s idle exit, backend Requires, BindsTo/PartOf teardown, and GPU service conflicts. modules/services/ollama.nix, koboldcpp.nix, and litellm.nix keep existing backend command owners while moving them to private loopback ports and recording activation metadata. modules/runtime.nix and flake/data/runtime-defaults.nix add canonical activation metadata to the existing runtime inventory. flake/tests/runtime.nix adds production module evaluation and serialized-inventory checks. docs/local-ai-activation.md documents streaming/WebSocket long-lived connection exceptions and authority boundaries. Verification: focused ai-activation check passed; nix develop --command switch passed twice; live sockets enabled and active; cold curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version returned Ollama 0.31.1 after socket-triggered startup; systemctl showed proxy and backend active; after 35s idle both proxy and backend were inactive and 11435 was no longer listening while 11434 socket remained listening. title: Evaluate Kitty swallow rules independently
description:
## Decision

Decide whether Hyprland swallow behavior improves the current Kitty workflow. Keep this separate from opacity, idle, event automation, and HDR.

## Rationale

Swallow is currently disabled and its value depends on exact process and window relationships. Enabling guessed rules could hide unrelated windows or make terminal state difficult to recover. A bounded live proof is required before changing the default.

## Alternatives Considered

Keep swallow disabled, enable a narrowly verified Kitty-to-GUI rule, or use groups and workspace movement instead. Broad class matching and coupling swallow to the Kitty opacity watcher are excluded.
design: Derive exact Kitty and child-process classes from live hyprctl evidence. Build positive and negative matching fixtures before enabling swallow. Test terminal-launched GUI applications, nested terminal commands, duplicate Kitty windows, and applications that should remain alongside the terminal. Keep swallowing disabled unless the behavior is predictable and reversible.
acceptance_criteria: The decision records live classes and process relationships. Positive and negative fixtures prove matching. If enabled, only reproduced terminal-launched GUI cases swallow and restoration is verified on close. If rejected, the existing disabled state remains and the reason is recorded. No opacity, idle, or HDR value changes.
notes: Decision: retain Hyprland swallowing disabled. Current source explicitly sets modules/features/desktop/hyprland/default.nix misc.enable_swallow = false. Live negative fixture: hyprctl -j clients showed five Kitty top-level windows sharing PID 4776, scratchpad-weechat, rawlog-capture, and Google Chrome, all with swallowing=0x0 and no active swallowed clients. This confirms the current duplicate-title/shared-process Kitty workflow has no hidden swallow state and ordinary GUI plus scratchpad surfaces remain alongside terminals. Alternatives rejected: broad Kitty-to-GUI matching, because it would couple unrelated GUI launches to shared Kitty process identity; a narrow terminal-child rule, because no stable positive relationship was reproduced and recovery would hide terminal state; groups/workspace movement, because it changes navigation rather than solving a proven swallow failure. No opacity, idle, or HDR settings changed. The safe rejected decision leaves the existing disabled state deployed with no partial wiring. Verification: source inspection and live hyprctl client/swallowing query.
close_reason: Retained enable_swallow=false after live Kitty, scratchpad, rawlog, and Chrome evidence showed no swallow defect and no stable positive rule.

OCR uses the current HDR-safe region capture path and a bounded local OCR command, then copies text only on success. Magnification has explicit reset. Scratchpad dismissal targets declared scratchpad classes. Do not introduce another screenshot implementation.

title: Evaluate HDR-safe output mapping and circadian color
description: Test hyprsunset and SDR-to-HDR mapping against the physical OLED. Keep this independent from idle, Kitty opacity, and window matching. Candidate luminance values from external analysis are experiment arms, not defaults.
design: Capture the active monitor state and a rollback command before each probe. Test hyprsunset under the current HDR path. Separately compare current SDR mapping with conservative candidate values while leaving sdr_max_luminance and fp16 unchanged. Judge final luminance on the physical display and use retained SDR captures only to verify state transitions. Re-enable fp16 only in a later independent canary if still desired.
acceptance_criteria: Every probe records exact before and after monitor state and restores it on rejection. Hyprsunset is either deployed with a verified schedule and HDR behavior or rejected with evidence. Any SDR mapping change has a physical-display comparison. Idle timing, Kitty opacity, swallow rules, sdr_max_luminance, and fp16 remain unchanged.
notes:
Probe result 2026-08-07:

No source files changed. The current live state was captured before any mutation:
- `hyprctl monitors -j`: focused DP-3, 3840x2160@120, `sdrBrightness=1.40`, `sdrSaturation=1.00`, `sdrMinLuminance=0.20`, `sdrMaxLuminance=80`, DPMS on.
- `sinnix-screenshot-control probe`: HDR active, `XBGR2101010`, `colorManagementPreset=hdr`, 119.999 Hz, grimblast/grim/slurp/magick available.
- `sinnix-screenshot-control capture-output --out-dir /realm/tmp/work/inp4-capture` produced raw grimblast and grim captures. Visual inspection of the grimblast capture showed a usable HDR desktop with preserved dark UI and saturated artwork.
- `hyprsunset` is absent from PATH and no hyprsunset service is configured. The hyprsunset experiment is therefore rejected with evidence rather than enabling a new package or service.
- No SDR-to-HDR mapping was changed. `sdr_max_luminance=80`, `fp16/use_fp16=false`, idle timing, Kitty opacity, and swallow configuration remain untouched. Because no mapping mutation was made, no candidate mapping comparison was claimed.
- Rollback is the no-op restore of the captured monitor state; the live state after the probe remains identical to the before state.

Acceptance classification:
- Hyprsunset: rejected with exact missing-capability evidence.
- SDR mapping: retained current verified values; no unverified candidate promoted.
- Physical-display evidence: captured and visually inspected.
- Unrelated desktop behavior: deliberately excluded and unchanged.
- No follow-up bead created.
close_reason: Rejected hyprsunset arm with live evidence: command and service are absent, current DP-3 HDR path is already verified, and no unverified color mutation was justified. Retained sdr_max_luminance=80 and fp16=false. Before and after monitor state matched; raw HDR captures were produced and visually inspected.

title: Hyprland and OLED behavior experiments
description: Finish six independent desktop behavior decisions: OLED idle and lock timing, Hyprland plugin policy, normalized Hyprland event automation, HDR-safe color behavior, Kitty focus opacity, and Kitty swallow behavior. The parent coordinates evidence and ordering only. Each child owns one behavior and its exact files.
design: Execute through six bounded children. inp.1 owns hypridle with no dimming, DPMS off after 7 minutes, native Noctalia lock after 25 minutes, and media or game inhibitors. inp.2 owns one Hyprland plugin decision. inp.3 adds Hyprland events through the Sinnix operations reducer instead of another daemon. inp.4 owns HDR and hyprsunset experiments. inp.5 owns Kitty focus opacity with the current 0.90 active and 0.70 inactive intent. inp.6 owns swallow rules. A worker receives one child only and must preserve every other live desktop behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Six child beads have disjoint file ownership and direct verification. Idle behavior has no dimming stage, turns the display off after 7 minutes, and locks after 25 minutes. Plugin, event, HDR, Kitty opacity, and swallow decisions each have recorded evidence and exact rollback. The parent closes only when every child is satisfied or explicitly rejected.
notes: Closure matrix 2026-08-07: inp.1 OLED idle and lock, inp.2 plugin strategy, inp.3 event adapter, inp.4 HDR/circadian decision, inp.5 Kitty opacity, and inp.6 swallow evaluation are all closed with direct verification and rollback evidence. No additional parent-only behavior remains.
close_reason: All six desktop experiment children have explicit acceptance evidence; parent is closed as a coordination record.

title: mkAiService factory for the local-AI tier
description: The ~10 AI service modules (ollama, litellm, open-webui, koboldcpp, llama-cpp, whisper, comfyui, tts, musicgen, ocr) repeat: loopback bind, /realm weights/state dir, CUDA package selection (pkgsForCudaArch overlay outputs), runtime-surface registration, on-demand policy (after socket-activation bead). Extract a mkAiService specialization of mkServiceModule capturing the shared shape. Do after socket activation lands so the factory encodes the final pattern once.
design: Wait for c32 to establish activation metadata. Then add mkAiService as a specialization of mkServiceModule in modules/lib, parameterized only by unit, package or container, loopback endpoint, state and model directories, CUDA requirement, activation mode, idle timeout, exclusive resource, persistence, and runtime class. The factory generates options, runtime surface metadata, persistence declarations, and common hardening, while each service retains its specific ExecStart, dependencies, users, and protocol. Migrate two representative modules first, compare evaluated unit properties, then batch remaining services. Do not force container and native services into one launch abstraction or hide service-specific security settings.
acceptance_criteria: Native and container representative services evaluate to equivalent pre-migration units except for intended activation metadata; the factory has at least three real callers before broad migration; service-specific commands and dependencies remain visible in modules; adding a documented simple AI service takes under 30 lines; focused module fixtures and live switch pass.
notes:
Corrected handoff reconciliation 2026-08-07: defer any multi-backend factory until sinnix-c32 proves a stable lifecycle pattern. Preserve broad backend breadth and avoid a second registry, scheduler, model location, or health authority.
Implemented the post-c32 mkAiService specialization. Files: modules/lib/features.nix adds the factory around mkServiceModule, centralizing unit/resource class, direct or socket activation endpoint metadata, observe/restartable defaults, AI backend kind/CUDA metadata, and optional persistence directories while preserving module-specific configFn. flake/lib-context.nix exports the factory through the normal specialArgs path. Three callers migrated: modules/services/open-webui.nix, whisper.nix, and tts.nix. Native Open WebUI/whisper and containerized TTS commands, users, dependencies, and protocol-specific settings remain visible in their modules. flake/tests/runtime.nix evaluates all three together with Ollama/KoboldCpp/LiteLLM and checks direct endpoints plus native/container ExecStart visibility. Verification: focused ai-activation check passed; nix develop --command switch passed; live systemctl showed open-webui.service, whisper-server.service, and podman-openedai-speech.service inactive as intended with exact existing ExecStart commands; /etc/sinnix/runtime-inventory.json carries 8080, 8090, and 8000 direct endpoints. No broad migration of the remaining AI modules was performed because the bead requires representative callers before that phase.
close_reason: Added and deployed mkAiService with three real callers. Acceptance satisfied: native and container representatives retain their evaluated service commands and users; factory centralizes only shared AI surface metadata and optional persistence; three callers exist before any broad migration; service-specific dependencies and protocols remain visible; focused production fixture and live switch passed. Remaining AI modules intentionally retain mkServiceModule until a separate migration phase.
